## Prices and offers

Source: https://marieglowstudio.com/pricing.md

Marie Glow Studio is a digital studio in Wichita, KS that helps product and service small businesses with web design and development, Pinterest marketing, SEO and digital strategy. All prices in USD. Every price is also listed on its own service page at https://marieglowstudio.com/services.

### Web Design & Development

#### Website Starter
- Price: $249 (one-time)
- Delivery: 5 business days from completed intake, guaranteed, or the revision round is free
- Works for: a shop or a service business (buy button, booking link, quote form or call button)
- Includes: professionally designed mobile-responsive one-page website customized to your brand colors/fonts/logo/photos/copy, basic on-page SEO, contact section with social links, domain-connection assistance, basic pre-launch testing, one revision round
- Add-ons: extra pages $79 each; Light-Edit Care Plan (first 30 days free, then $25/edit or $15/month for up to two)
- Not included: e-commerce, custom photography or copywriting, unlimited revisions
- Upgrade path: $100 of what you paid is credited toward the Complete Package if you upgrade within 6 months
- Checkout: https://buy.stripe.com/cNi7sMd101Hi7x68j83VC05

#### Complete Website & Brand Identity
- Price: $1,497 (one-time)
- Delivery: roughly 2-3 weeks depending on how quickly product images/content are provided
- Includes: custom primary logo, brand colors, font recommendations, visual brand direction, style guide, social media graphics, full site build (Shopify for online stores, custom-coded for service businesses), custom homepage, mobile-responsive layout, essential pages, navigation, product/collection organization for up to 20 items, contact form, footer, policy pages, domain support, full store review/testing/training
- Credit: the $397 Digital Strategy Roadmap is credited toward this package if booked within 60 days
- Refund policy: non-refundable once work begins
- Checkout: https://buy.stripe.com/28E3cwgdc3Pq7x6czo3VC06

### Pinterest Marketing

#### Pinterest SEO Audit
- Price: $197 (one-time)
- Delivery: single document within 4 business days
- Includes: full review of profile, bio, boards, board titles/descriptions, keywords, existing pins, pin titles/descriptions, account organization, website connection, content alignment, and analytics, plus a ranked 30-day action plan
- Not included: hands-on implementation
- Checkout: https://buy.stripe.com/dRm9AU9OO2Lm7x60QG3VC00

#### Pinterest Business Account Setup & SEO Optimization
- Price: $497 (one-time)
- Delivery: 10-15 business days after all required information is received
- Includes: created or optimized Pinterest business account, SEO-focused profile optimization, keyword research, competitor analysis, content pillar development, board strategy across up to 10 boards, 10 custom pins with SEO titles/descriptions/alt text/UTM tracking, website connection support, store or website integration review, Rich Pin/catalog readiness check, Tailwind setup review, 30-day launch plan
- Not included: ongoing posting (see Monthly Pinterest Management)
- Checkout: https://buy.stripe.com/28E6oI9OOclWaJi42S3VC01

#### Monthly Pinterest Management
- Billing: monthly, no minimum commitment, cancel anytime
- Core inclusions on every tier: monthly account management, keyword research, content planning, custom branded pin graphics with SEO titles/descriptions, alt text and SEO-friendly filenames, UTM tracking, destination-link review, recommended board placement, Pinterest/Tailwind scheduling, board maintenance, broken-link monitoring, monthly analytics review and performance summary, one revision round, email support

| Tier | Price | Pins/month | Added on top of core |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pinterest Starter | $497/mo | 100 | none |
| Pinterest Growth (Most Popular) | $797/mo | 200 | Expanded keyword targeting, enhanced analytics reporting, priority content planning |
| Pinterest Pro | $1,097/mo | 300 | Advanced content planning, broader keyword targeting, detailed monthly analytics, one monthly strategy call, priority email support |

- Checkout, one link per tier: Starter https://buy.stripe.com/6oU9AU6CC85GbNmgPE3VC02 , Growth https://buy.stripe.com/3cI7sMaSSgCc18I1UK3VC03 , Pro https://buy.stripe.com/4gMeVe8KKclWeZyeHw3VC04

### SEO

#### Website SEO Audit
- Price: $247 (one-time)
- Delivery: about 7 business days
- Includes: technical check (speed, mobile, indexing, broken links, sitemap and robots), on-page review (titles, headings, meta descriptions, internal links), local SEO check (Google Business Profile, name/address/phone consistency, local keywords), AI-search readiness (schema, FAQ structure, entity clarity), and a written, prioritized fix list
- Not included: implementing the fixes (see SEO Foundations Setup)
- Checkout: https://buy.stripe.com/6oU28saSS1HiaJidDs3VC07

#### SEO Foundations Setup
- Price: $697 (one-time)
- Scope: up to 10 pages
- Includes: keyword map, titles and meta descriptions, schema markup, Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools setup, sitemap, internal linking, Google Business Profile optimization
- No ranking guarantees; this builds the foundation search engines and AI assistants need to understand the site
- Checkout: https://buy.stripe.com/28EbJ28KKeu42cMdDs3VC08

### Digital Strategy

#### Digital Strategy Roadmap
- Price: $397 (one-time)
- Delivery: within 10 business days once everything needed to begin has been received. The project timeline begins only after all required content, information, files and access have been received. It does not start on the purchase date or first contact, and time spent waiting on the client (information, content, branding or assets, photos or files, logins or access, or other required materials) does not count. Confirmed by Marie on 2026-09-26. This clock-start rule applies to the Digital Strategy Roadmap only; it has not been extended to any other offer.
- Includes: a map of how customers move across the website, search, Pinterest, email and tools; where they drop off today; a written 90-day plan with priorities; a walkthrough
- Credit: the full $397 is credited toward the Complete Website & Brand Identity package if booked within 60 days
- Checkout: https://buy.stripe.com/3cIeVe2mm5Xy9Feczo3VC09

What your website is for

#### Looking good is the starting line. Getting chosen is the job.

- 01

#### Easier to find

You show up on Google, on Pinterest and in AI answers when someone searches for what you sell or the service you offer, including the searches that end in “near me.”

- 02

#### Easier to understand

Within a few seconds on your site, a visitor knows what you do, who it is for and where you work. No guessing, no digging through menus.

- 03

#### Easier to choose

Reviews, photos of real work, clear prices and a site that holds up on a phone. The small signals that make someone trust you over the next result.

- 04

#### Easier to say yes

Buy, book, call, ask for a quote or join your list. Whatever a yes looks like for your business, the next step is right there.

In their words

Questions

#### What people usually ask before they reach out.

[Read every FAQ →](https://marieglowstudio.com/faqs)

**What is Marie Glow Studio?**

Marie Glow Studio is a digital studio in Wichita, KS that helps product and service small businesses with web design and development, Pinterest marketing, SEO and digital strategy. The work is done by one person, start to finish, so your website, search visibility and marketing are planned together instead of in separate pieces.

**Do you only build Shopify websites?**

No. Shopify is one option, and it is usually the right one for an online store. Service businesses often do better with a fast custom-coded site connected to their booking tool or quote form. The business problem decides the platform, not the other way around.

**Do you work with service businesses, or only product businesses?**

Both. A product business needs a clear path from discovery to checkout. A service business needs a clear path from discovery to an inquiry, a call or a booking. Every site and strategy is built around the way your own customers actually say yes.

**Do I need all four services?**

No. Most businesses start with the one piece that is holding them back the most, often a website or an audit. The four services are designed to connect, so anything added later fits what is already built instead of starting over.

**How much does it cost to work with Marie Glow Studio?**

Audits start at $197 for Pinterest and $247 for website SEO. The Website Starter is $249, SEO Foundations Setup is $697, and the Complete Website and Brand Identity package is $1,497. Monthly Pinterest management runs $497 to $1,097. Every price is listed on its service page.

**Do you only work with businesses in Wichita?**

No. Marie Glow Studio is based in Wichita, Kansas and works remotely with small businesses across the United States. Local Wichita businesses get the same service, plus local SEO that is built with the area in mind.

Start here

Questions

#### What people usually ask before they book.

[Read every FAQ →](https://marieglowstudio.com/faqs)

**Where do I start if I need everything?**

Start with the Digital Strategy Roadmap or one of the two audits. Both are built to show you exactly which service will move the needle first, so you are not guessing or buying everything at once.

**Do the four services have to be bought together?**

No. Most people start with one piece, usually a website or an audit, and add the others later. Every service is built to connect with the others, so nothing you buy first gets wasted.

**What is the difference between the two audits?**

The Pinterest SEO Audit reviews your Pinterest account, keywords, boards and pins. The Website SEO Audit reviews your website itself: technical health, on-page SEO, local SEO and AI-search readiness. Many businesses need both, but they solve different problems.

**How fast do these services get delivered?**

The Pinterest SEO Audit is delivered within 4 business days and the Website SEO Audit in about 7 business days. The Website Starter is live in about five business days from a completed intake. Pinterest Account Setup takes 10 to 15 business days after everything is received, and the Complete Website & Brand Identity package usually takes two to three weeks, depending on how quickly your photos and content arrive. The Digital Strategy Roadmap is within 10 business days once everything needed to begin has been received. Each service page lists its own timeline.

#### Small business website design that gets you chosen, not just seen.

A small business website earns its keep when it turns a visitor into a customer. If you sell products, that means a fast Shopify store built to check out. If you run a service, that means a custom-coded site built to get booked, quoted or called. Either way, one designer plans the whole thing around how your own customers say yes, starting at $249.

#### Products organized to be found

The information a buyer needs before they trust a small shop with their card, laid out where they actually look for it.

#### Checkout without friction

A cart and checkout flow that does not lose people between "add to cart" and "order confirmed."

In their words

Questions

#### Before you pick a starting point.

**Do you only build Shopify websites?**

No. Shopify is the right platform for an online store, so product businesses build there. Service businesses usually do better with a fast, custom-coded site connected to their booking tool, quote form or phone number. The business decides the platform, not the other way around.

**How do I know if I need the Starter or the Complete Package?**

Start with the Website Starter at $249 if you need one clear, professional page live fast, no e-commerce required. Move to the Complete Website & Brand Identity Package at $1,497 if you are launching or relaunching a full store or a multi-page service site with branding included.

**Can I upgrade from the Starter later?**

Yes. Upgrade to the Complete Website & Brand Identity Package within 6 months of your Starter purchase and $100 of what you paid is credited toward it.

**Do you write the copy for my site?**

You provide the copy for the Website Starter. Copywriting is not included in the Website Starter. If you need copy help with the Complete Package, ask before you buy. Either way, nothing goes live without your review.

**What if I sell products and also take bookings?**

Tell me both during intake. Most hybrid businesses still lead with one path, usually checkout or booking, and the site is built around whichever one makes you the most money.

A right-sized first step

#### You do not need a huge site to look professional.

A focused one-page site gives a visitor everything they need to trust you: who you are, what you offer, proof of your work, and a clear way to reach you. Starting here means your website stops waiting on you, whether the next step is a purchase, a booking or a call.

The package

#### What’s included.

Included

#### Everything a first real website needs

A professionally designed, mobile-responsive one-page site, customized with your brand colors, fonts and logo, built with your photos and copy. Basic on-page SEO (heading structure, page title, meta description, image alt text), a contact section with your social links, domain-connection assistance, pre-launch testing, and one revision round.

Not included: multiple pages (add for $79 each), e-commerce, custom photography or copywriting, extensive custom graphics, or unlimited revisions. Anything past this scope moves into the Complete Website & Brand Identity Package.

The promise

#### Delivered in 5 business days, guaranteed.

Complete your intake and your site is live within five business days, or your revision round is on the house.

Not a social feed

#### People use Pinterest to decide, not to scroll.

- 01

#### It works for products

Shops, makers and product brands use Pinterest for exactly the searches you would expect: gift ideas, seasonal products, “outfits for,” “gifts for.” A pin points straight to the product or collection that matches.

- 02

#### It works for services too

Someone planning a wedding searches Pinterest for venues and florists. Someone renovating a bathroom searches for tile ideas and contractors. Salons, planners, coaches and home-service businesses all show up in the same kind of inspiration search, months before that person is ready to book.

- 03

#### It keeps paying off

A social post is seen for a day or two. A well-built pin, with the right title, description and keywords, keeps getting found in search for months after you publish it.

- 04

#### It feeds your website

Every pin should land on the exact page that matches what someone searched: a product, a service page, a blog post or a booking link. Pinterest is the discovery layer that sends people to the site that closes the sale.

Three parts of SEO

#### Search visibility is more than Google now.

A page that isn’t built to rank, isn’t built to show up locally, and isn’t built to be read by AI is losing traffic in three different places at once.

- 01

#### Website SEO: is your site built to be found?

Page speed, mobile usability, indexing, broken links and a working sitemap, plus on-page basics like titles, headings, meta descriptions and internal links pointing to the right pages.

- 02

#### Local SEO: do you show up for “near me”?

Your Google Business Profile, Google Maps listing and NAP (name, address, phone) consistency across the web. Marie Glow Studio is based in Wichita, KS and builds local SEO for businesses there, plus service-area setups for clients across the United States.

- 03

#### Answer-engine optimization: can AI find and quote you correctly?

Schema markup, FAQ content written the way people actually ask questions, and one consistent set of facts about your business, so tools like ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini describe you accurately instead of guessing.

Who this is for

#### A shop and a service business are chasing different searches.

SEO work only helps when it’s built around what your customer is actually typing.

If you sell products

#### Searches that end in a purchase

- “handmade lavender candles near me”

- Product and collection pages built with real titles and descriptions

- Schema that tells Google and AI what you sell and at what price

- Blog and guide content that answers buying questions

Shops, makers, handmade brands, boutiques and digital products.

If you sell a service

#### Searches that end in a call or booking

- “HVAC repair Wichita KS” or “esthetician near me”

- A dedicated page for every service you offer

- A Google Business Profile that matches your website exactly

- FAQ content that answers the questions people ask before they book

Salons, spas, contractors, home services, coaches and consultants.

No promises, just work

#### No one can promise you a ranking.

Search engines and AI models change constantly, and anyone guaranteeing a specific rank is guessing along with you. What you get instead is honest, prioritized work: the real problems fixed in the order that matters most.

Questions

#### What people usually ask about SEO.

[Read every FAQ →](https://marieglowstudio.com/faqs)

**Will SEO get my website to the top of Google?**

No one can honestly promise that, and any studio that does is overselling you. What SEO work can do is fix the technical and content problems that are actively keeping you out of search results and AI answers, so you are competing on a level field instead of an uneven one.

**What is local SEO, and do I need it?**

Local SEO is the set of signals, like your Google Business Profile, map listing and address consistency, that help you show up for searches with a location in them, including “near me.” If customers find you in person, by phone or through a service area, local SEO is worth doing alongside your general website SEO.

**What is answer-engine optimization, or AEO?**

AEO is making it easy for AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini to understand and quote your business correctly. That means clear schema markup, FAQ content written in plain language, and consistent facts about who you are and what you do across your site.

**Do you only work with product businesses, or service businesses too?**

Both. A product business is usually optimizing for searches like “handmade lavender candles” that end in a purchase. A service business is usually optimizing for searches like “HVAC repair near me” that end in a call or a booking. The SEO work is built around which one applies to you.

**What SEO services does Marie Glow Studio offer?**

A Website SEO Audit for $247 that reviews your site and hands you a prioritized fix list, and an SEO Foundations Setup for $697 that implements the keyword map, titles and meta descriptions, schema markup, Search Console and Bing setup, a sitemap, internal linking and Google Business Profile optimization for up to 10 pages.

A few lines about your business is plenty. I read every message myself and reply within one to two business days with an honest recommendation, even if it is the smallest option.

### Page: Digital Strategy for Small Business

URL: https://marieglowstudio.com/digital-strategy

Digital Strategy

#### Your website, search, Pinterest and email are already one customer journey.

Digital strategy is the plain-English map of how those pieces pass a person along today, where they get stuck or drop off, and what to fix first. It is not more jargon on top of what you already have. It is the thing that tells you which piece to work on next.

[See the Digital Strategy Roadmap, $397](https://marieglowstudio.com/digital-strategy-roadmap)
[Compare every service](https://marieglowstudio.com/services)

5

Channels mapped: website, search, Pinterest, email, tools

90

Day written plan, with priorities in order

1

Walkthrough call to go over it together

In plain English

#### Five channels, one job each, and one job connecting them.

You probably already have most of these pieces. Strategy is just making sure each one hands the person to the next instead of leaving them stranded.

- 01

#### Website

The destination. Where someone finally decides yes or no, so it has to load fast, explain what you do, and give a clear next step.

- 02

#### Search

How Google, Bing and AI answers find and describe you. If your pages do not answer the actual question someone typed, they never get this far.

- 03

#### Pinterest

Discovery for people still planning what to buy, make or book. A pin’s only job is to send the right person to the right page.

- 04

#### Email

The follow-up. It brings back the person who almost said yes, and it is usually the cheapest leak to fix.

- 05

#### Tools

Booking links, quote forms, checkout, your CRM. The small connections between channels that quietly break more often than the channels themselves.

The four shapes

#### Every business fits one of these journeys, or a mix of two.

The map looks different for a shop than it does for a coach, but the idea is the same: find where the path is clear, and where it breaks.

Product business

#### From discovery to a repeat order

- Discovery on Pinterest or search

- Lands on the right product page

- Cart, with nothing slowing checkout down

- Purchase completes without friction

- Retention: email brings them back

Shops, makers, handmade brands, boutiques and digital products.

[Websites for product businesses →](https://marieglowstudio.com/for-product-businesses)

Service business

#### From discovery to a booked client

- Discovery through local search, Maps or referral

- Lands on the right service page

- Trust: reviews and photos of real work

- Inquiry: a call, quote request or message

- Booking confirms the appointment or project

Salons, spas, contractors, home services, coaches and consultants.

[Websites for service businesses →](https://marieglowstudio.com/for-service-businesses)

Local business

#### From a nearby search to a visit

- Search or Maps for a “near me” term

- Reviews and photos decide who gets picked

- A call or a visit, often the same day

Restaurants, retail storefronts, studios and any business people drive to.

Course or coach

#### From content to a paying client

- Content: a blog post, pin or video that helps first

- Lead magnet trades a next step for an email

- Email nurtures with more useful content

- Offer: the course, program or coaching call

Coaches, course creators and anyone selling knowledge or guidance.

Where people usually leak

#### Not the whole system. Almost always one weak link.

A pin sending traffic to the homepage instead of the product. A service page with no way to book. An email list that never hears from you again after the first message. The roadmap finds the leak that is actually costing you customers, so you fix that first instead of guessing.

The roadmap

#### Digital Strategy Roadmap

A customer-journey map across your website, search, Pinterest, email and tools, where people are dropping off today, and a written 90-day plan with priorities, walked through with you.

Questions

#### What people ask before starting a roadmap.

**What does digital strategy actually mean?**

It means looking at your website, search visibility, Pinterest, email and any tools you use as one connected path instead of separate projects, then finding the exact spot where people are dropping off before they buy, book or reach out.

**Do I need a full rebuild to fix my digital strategy?**

Usually not. Most businesses have one or two real leaks, not a broken system. A roadmap tells you which piece to fix first, and often that is a page, an email sequence or a missing link, not a full rebuild.

**How is this different from an SEO or Pinterest audit?**

An SEO or Pinterest audit looks closely at one channel. A digital strategy roadmap looks at how all of your channels connect and hand a visitor off to the next step, so you can see the whole path a customer takes, not just one piece of it.

**What do I get at the end?**

A customer-journey map of your website, search, Pinterest, email and tools, a written list of where people are dropping off today, and a 90-day plan with priorities, walked through with you.

### How to Measure Small Business Marketing

URL: https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/how-to-measure-small-business-marketing
Topic: Digital Strategy | Published: 2026-09-25

A small business can measure its marketing with a short list of numbers: website visits and where they came from, how many people search and find you, Google Business Profile activity, and how many inquiries or bookings actually happen. A simple monthly review of these beats a dozen dashboards nobody opens.

Coaches, salons and other service businesses often skip measurement entirely, because the tools feel built for online stores. Most of what matters is free to set up and takes only a few minutes to check each month.

#### What should a small business actually track each month?

Track the numbers that connect directly to a sale or a booking, not every metric a tool offers. For most small businesses, that is a short list:

- Website visits and their source, from Google Analytics 4
- Search performance, from Google Search Console
- Local visibility, from Google Business Profile insights
- Pinterest impressions, saves and outbound clicks, from Pinterest analytics
- Actual inquiries or bookings, from your booking tool or contact form

#### Do you need every tool on this list on day one?

No. Start with whichever tool matches the channel you already have running. A service business with only a Google Business Profile and a booking tool does not need GA4 or Pinterest analytics yet, since there is nothing else to measure. Add a tool only when you add the channel it measures, so each new number you track already connects to something you are actively doing, instead of sitting in a dashboard nobody has time to check.

#### What does Google Analytics 4 tell you that Search Console does not?

Google Analytics 4, usually called GA4, shows what happens after someone arrives on your site: which pages they visit, how they got there, and whether they took an action like submitting a form or reaching checkout. Search Console shows what happens before that, in Google search itself, including which queries show your site and how often people click. The two answer different questions, and a monthly review benefits from checking both.

#### What does Google Business Profile insight show?

For a local or service business, Google Business Profile shows how often your listing appeared in search and maps, how many people called, requested directions or visited your website from the listing, directly from a real, free source. For a salon, contractor or clinic, this number often matters more than website traffic alone, because it reflects people actively looking to book nearby.

#### How do you track bookings and inquiries?

Through whatever tool actually takes the booking. Scheduling tools such as Square Appointments, Acuity Scheduling and Calendly keep their own count of bookings and cancellations, and a simple contact form should log or email every submission so nothing gets lost. The table below matches the number to the tool that provides it.

| What you want to know | Where to look | What it tells you |
| Where visitors come from | Google Analytics 4 | Which channel is actually sending people to the site |
| What people search to find you | Google Search Console | The exact queries and pages that show up in search results |
| Local search activity | Google Business Profile insights | Calls, direction requests and website clicks from the listing |
| Pinterest performance | Pinterest analytics | Impressions, saves and outbound clicks per pin |
| Real inquiries and bookings | Booking tool or contact form log | Whether traffic is turning into actual appointments or messages |

#### How do you turn these numbers into an actual decision?

Compare each number to itself over time, not to another business's numbers or to a number you saw in an article. If Search Console clicks are climbing steadily but bookings are flat, the leak is probably somewhere between the website and the booking step, not in search itself. If Pinterest impressions are high but outbound clicks are low, the pins are being seen but not convincing anyone to leave Pinterest, which points at the pin copy or image rather than the topic. Looking at the numbers together, instead of one at a time, is usually what turns a report into a decision about what to fix.

#### How do you track Pinterest performance specifically?

Pinterest's own analytics show impressions, saves and outbound clicks for each pin and board, which is enough for most small businesses to see which topics and formats are working. Watch outbound clicks especially, since impressions and saves show interest but outbound clicks show someone actually leaving Pinterest for your site.

#### What should a coach or service business track that a product shop might skip?

Booking and inquiry counts matter more for a coach or a service business than raw traffic does, since the business only succeeds when a visitor actually books a call or a session. A coaching website can show healthy traffic and still be failing if very few visitors ever inquire, which is why the inquiry and booking numbers deserve more attention than page views alone. Watching how many people view a service page compared with how many actually submit a form or book a call, sometimes called a conversion rate even without any software to calculate it, tells you far more than traffic by itself.

#### What does a simple monthly review look like?

Set a recurring time, even fifteen minutes, to check the same five numbers every month: GA4 visits and source, Search Console clicks, Google Business Profile activity, Pinterest outbound clicks, and real bookings or inquiries. Write down anything that moved a lot, up or down, and ask why before changing anything. [The Customer Journey for Service Businesses, Step by Step](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/customer-journey-for-service-businesses) covers where in that journey each number tends to shift, and [What Is Digital Strategy for a Small Business?](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/what-is-digital-strategy-for-small-business) explains how these numbers tie back to your website, search, Pinterest and email as one system. If a monthly review feels like too much to set up alone, the [Digital Strategy Roadmap](https://marieglowstudio.com/digital-strategy-roadmap) from Marie Glow Studio maps this out for you once, with a written plan you can keep reusing.

#### Frequently asked questions

**Do I need Google Analytics if I already have Search Console?**

Both are useful and they answer different questions, so most small businesses benefit from checking each. Search Console shows how you appear in Google search results and which queries find you, while GA4 shows what visitors actually do after they reach your website, including which pages they leave from.

**How do I measure marketing if I do not sell online?**

Track inquiries, calls and bookings instead of purchases, since those are the actions that matter for a service business. Google Business Profile insights and your booking tool's own reporting usually tell a salon, contractor or coach most of what a monthly review needs, without any extra software.

**What is a good number of website visits for a small business?**

There is no universal good number, and comparing your traffic to another business rarely helps. The more useful comparison is your own trend over time, and whether the visits you do get are actually turning into inquiries, bookings or sales, which matters far more than the raw visit count.

**How often should I check my marketing numbers?**

Monthly works well for most small businesses, since it is frequent enough to catch a real problem early without reacting to normal day to day noise. Checking only once a year makes it much harder to notice a drop in traffic or bookings before it has already cost you customers.

**Which number matters most if I can only check one?**

Real inquiries or bookings. Traffic, impressions and saves are useful context for understanding why a number moved, but the single number that reflects actual business results is how many people took the final step, whether that is a purchase, a booking or a message asking to work with you.

### Answer Engine Optimization for Small Business: A Plain Guide

URL: https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/answer-engine-optimization-for-small-business
Topic: SEO and Search Visibility | Published: 2026-09-22

Answer engine optimization, or AEO, is the practice of making your business easy for AI tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews to find, understand and quote correctly. It relies on clear schema markup, plainly written FAQ content, and one consistent set of facts about your business repeated across your site.

Traditional SEO earns you a place in a list of ten blue links. Answer engines skip the list and hand the searcher a direct answer, sometimes with your business named and sometimes not. Being the source an AI tool actually pulls from is a different, newer kind of visibility, and it rewards clarity over cleverness.

#### What is answer engine optimization?

It is the set of practices that help AI systems extract accurate facts from your website: your prices, your services, your location, your hours, your policies. Where traditional SEO optimizes for a ranking position, AEO optimizes for being correctly understood, since an AI tool that misreads your page will confidently repeat the mistake to anyone who asks.

#### How do tools like ChatGPT and Perplexity actually find business information?

Different tools work differently. Some, like Perplexity and Google AI Overviews, search the live web in real time and cite sources directly. Others rely more on training data or a combination of both. Across all of them, clear, well structured, plainly worded content is easier to pull an accurate answer from than a vague page full of marketing language.

#### Does schema markup actually matter for AI answers?

Yes. Schema markup is structured data added to a page's code, invisible to visitors, that spells out facts in a format machines can parse without guessing: this is a Service, this Service costs this Price, this business is Open these Hours. FAQPage schema in particular gives AI tools a ready made question and answer pair to lift directly.

#### What should a small business actually do about AEO?

A handful of concrete steps cover most of it:

- Write real FAQ content in plain language, matching how customers actually ask questions

- Add schema markup for your organization, services and FAQs

- State your prices, location, hours and policies the same way everywhere on your site

- Answer the question directly in the first sentence or two of a page, before adding context

- Keep facts current, since an outdated price or hours listing gets repeated as fact

#### Is llms.txt worth setting up?

It is a reasonable, low effort step, with a caveat: llms.txt is a plain text file, similar in spirit to robots.txt, that some AI crawlers are beginning to check for a summary of a site's purpose and pages. It is an emerging convention, not yet a guaranteed standard every AI tool respects, so treat it as a helpful extra rather than a replacement for clear content and schema.

#### What does AI-search-ready content actually look like?

It answers the reader's question in the first sentence or two, in plain words, before adding supporting detail. Compare a vague opening like "we offer a range of solutions tailored to your needs" with a direct one like "a website starter site costs 249 dollars and takes about 5 business days." The second version gives an AI tool, and a human reader, something concrete to repeat correctly. FAQ sections are especially useful for this because the question-and-answer format is already close to how AI tools phrase their own responses.

#### How do I check that my schema markup actually works?

Google's Rich Results Test and the Schema.org validator both check a page's structured data for errors and confirm what a search engine or AI crawler can actually read from it. Run a page through one of these after any redesign or content change, since a broken script tag or a mismatched field can quietly invalidate the whole block without changing how the page looks to a visitor.

#### Does consistent business information really change anything?

It changes more than it seems like it should. When your price, hours, service area and policies are worded identically on your homepage, your service pages, your Google Business Profile and any directory listing, an AI tool has one clear fact to repeat instead of several conflicting versions to choose between. Inconsistency is often the quiet reason an AI answer gets your price or hours wrong even though the correct number appears somewhere on your site.

| Traditional SEO | Answer engine optimization |
| Optimizes for a ranking position in a results list | Optimizes for being the source an AI answer pulls from or cites |
| Keywords placed in titles, headings and body text | Plain, self contained answers a machine can lift without misreading |
| Backlinks and page authority matter heavily | Structured data and consistent facts matter alongside authority |

#### Who actually benefits most from AEO right now?

Businesses that answer a specific, well defined question tend to benefit fastest, since a narrow, clearly stated answer is exactly what an AI tool is looking to lift and repeat. A service business that clearly states its service area, pricing structure and process, or a product business that clearly states materials, sizing and care, gives an AI tool less room to guess and more reason to quote the page directly rather than paraphrase from somewhere less accurate.

#### Do I still need regular SEO if I do AEO?

Yes, and the two overlap more than they compete. A site with poor titles, no indexing and thin content, the kind of problems covered in [Why Your Website Is Not on Google](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/why-your-website-is-not-on-google), will struggle with AI visibility for the same underlying reasons it struggles with regular search. Fix the foundation first, then layer schema and FAQ content on top of it.

A [Website SEO Audit](https://marieglowstudio.com/website-seo-audit) reviews AI search readiness alongside the technical, on-page and local SEO basics, and [SEO Foundations Setup](https://marieglowstudio.com/seo-foundations) implements the schema markup, titles and structured content this depends on, for up to 10 pages.

#### Frequently asked questions

**Is answer engine optimization the same thing as SEO?**

They overlap heavily but are not identical. Traditional SEO earns a ranking position in a search results list, while answer engine optimization focuses on being the accurate source an AI tool pulls from or cites when it answers a question directly.

**Which AI tools should a small business worry about?**

ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity and Claude are the ones most likely to answer a customer’s question about a local business today. They work differently under the hood, but all of them respond better to clear, factual, plainly written pages than vague marketing copy.

**Can a small business really compete for AI visibility against big brands?**

Yes, more than in traditional search rankings. AI tools reward clarity and consistency over sheer size, so a small business with accurate schema, clear FAQ content and consistent facts can be quoted correctly even against much larger, less organized competitors.

**Do I need a developer to add schema markup?**

Not necessarily. Many platforms and plugins can generate basic schema automatically, but it still needs checking for accuracy against your real prices, hours and services. SEO Foundations Setup handles this directly if you would rather not manage it yourself.

**How do I know if AI tools are describing my business correctly?**

Ask the tools directly, the way a customer might, and read the answer closely. If the price, hours, location or services are wrong or outdated, that is a sign your website’s facts are inconsistent or your schema and FAQ content need attention.

### How Long Does It Take to Build a Website

URL: https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/how-long-does-it-take-to-build-a-website
Topic: Shopify and Web Design | Published: 2026-09-18

A simple one page website can go live in about five business days once content is ready, while a full brand identity paired with a multi page site usually takes two to three weeks. What matters most to the timeline is how quickly the business owner supplies content, photos and decisions.

Most delays on a website project are not design problems. They are waiting problems, waiting on a logo file, waiting on product photos, waiting on a decision about wording. Understanding that in advance is the fastest way to keep a project on schedule.

#### How long does a simple one page website take?

About five business days from a completed intake, for a straightforward one page site with existing branding and ready content. This works well for a shop or service business that needs one clear page with services, trust, contact and a call to action, not a large multi page structure.

#### How long does a full multi page website take?

Roughly two to three weeks for a custom multi page build that includes a brand identity, a homepage, several supporting pages, product or service organization and a full review before launch. This range still depends heavily on how quickly content, images and approvals come back during the process.

#### What happens during each phase of a website build?

Most builds move through the same rough phases, whether the site is one page or many: intake and planning, where scope and content get confirmed; design, where the layout and look come together; build, where the actual pages get put together and connected; and review, where the owner checks everything on a real phone and desktop before launch. A one page site moves through all four quickly since there is less to design and build. A multi page site with a full brand identity spends more time in design, since the logo, colors and style guide have to be settled before the pages can be built around them.

#### What actually slows a website build down?

- Missing or incomplete copy for key pages
- Product or service photos that still need to be taken or gathered
- Undecided branding, such as colors, fonts or a logo
- Slow turnaround on approving drafts or answering questions
- Adding new pages or features after the project has started
- Waiting on domain access or account logins needed to connect the site

#### How can a business owner speed things up?

Prepare as much as possible before the project starts. Gathering the essentials up front turns most of the timeline into design and build time instead of back and forth.

- Finalize copy, or at least rough notes, for every planned page
- Collect final photos, sized reasonably and in focus
- Settle on colors, fonts and a logo if the brand already has one
- List services or products with prices, descriptions and any variants
- Have domain and account access ready to hand over when asked
- Set aside time to review drafts quickly rather than letting them sit

#### Does the platform affect how long a website takes?

Somewhat, but less than most people expect. Shopify, for a store, and a custom-coded build, for a service business without e-commerce needs, both move at a similar pace once content is ready, because the platform mainly affects what is possible, not how fast pages get built. The real time difference comes from scope: number of pages, amount of custom design and how much content still needs to be written or gathered.

#### How many revision rounds should a website include?

Enough for the owner to catch real problems, without turning into an open-ended redesign. A single revision round after the first draft is common for a smaller project, covering wording changes, image swaps and small layout adjustments. Requests that change the scope, such as adding new pages or a different structure partway through, usually reset the timeline rather than fitting inside the original revision round.

#### What happens if content is not ready on time?

The timeline moves with it. A designer working from a written scope, such as a five business day guarantee, is usually counting from a completed intake, meaning the clock starts once the needed information arrives, not when the project is booked. [How Much Does a Small Business Website Cost](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/how-much-does-a-small-business-website-cost) covers how that same scope also drives price.

#### Does the time of year affect a website timeline?

Indirectly, through demand rather than the calendar itself. A designer or agency may book up before a busy retail season, so a business that waits until the last minute to start a project can find the earliest available start date is later than the stated turnaround. Starting the intake process early protects against that kind of scheduling delay, separate from the build time itself.

#### How should a business owner plan around the timeline?

Avoid booking a website build right before a launch, event or busy season unless there is real buffer time. Building in a week or two of slack protects against a normal delay, like a slow photo shoot, a late branding decision or a busy week that pushes a review back, without putting a hard deadline at risk.

Marie Glow Studio's [Website Starter](https://marieglowstudio.com/website-starter) is delivered within five business days of a completed intake, guaranteed, or the revision round is free. The [Complete Website and Brand Identity](https://marieglowstudio.com/complete-website-package) covers the fuller multi page timeline. [See both web design options together](https://marieglowstudio.com/web-design) to compare scope and timeline side by side.

#### Frequently asked questions

**How fast can a small business website go live?**

A simple one page site can go live in about five business days once all content is ready. A full multi page build with branding typically takes two to three weeks.

**What causes most website delays?**

Waiting on the business owner's content, photos, branding decisions or approvals, far more often than the design or build work itself.

**Can a website be built faster with a bigger budget?**

Sometimes, but content readiness usually matters more than budget. A rushed build with unclear content and photos rarely turns out well regardless of price.

**When should a business start a website project before a launch?**

Earlier than the minimum timeline suggests, with a week or two of buffer for normal delays like photo shoots, copy revisions or slow approvals.

### Where to Start With Small Business Marketing

URL: https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/where-to-start-with-small-business-marketing
Topic: Digital Strategy | Published: 2026-09-14

Start with one channel that matches how your customers already search or browse, and give it real time before adding another. Product businesses usually start with Pinterest or search, service businesses usually start with local search and their Google Business Profile, and almost nobody needs every channel running in the first year.

The most common marketing mistake for a small business is not picking the wrong channel. It is trying to run four channels at a quarter effort each, so none of them ever build enough momentum to work.

#### Where should a small business start with marketing?

Start with the channel where your customers are already looking for what you do, not the channel that feels the most exciting. A handmade product shop and a plumber are not looking for customers in the same place, so their first channel should not be the same either.

#### How do you choose your first marketing channel?

Answer three questions honestly, then pick the channel that fits the answers, not the one you feel you are supposed to be using.

- Where would a new customer naturally search for a business like yours
- How many hours a week can you actually give this, not in theory
- Do you have a website ready to receive the traffic once it arrives

If the honest answer to the third question is no, the real first step is the website, not the marketing channel that would send people to it.

#### What tools help you start with almost no budget?

Most starting channels are free at the setup stage, which is part of why they make sense as a first step. A Pinterest business account, a Google Business Profile and an email signup form can all be created without paying anyone. What costs money later, if it ever does, is speeding up results or handing the ongoing work to someone else once you know the channel works for your business. Starting free also removes the pressure to see an immediate return before you have even learned how the channel behaves for your specific audience.

#### Should a product business start differently than a service business?

Usually, yes. The table below shows a common starting point for each type, though a specific business can reasonably start elsewhere.

| Business type | Common first channel | Why |
| Product shop | Pinterest or Shopify SEO | Shoppers browse Pinterest while planning a purchase, and product SEO keeps working long after a post goes quiet |
| Local service business | Google Business Profile and local search | Most local searches include intent to book soon, so showing up there matters more than a general social presence |
| Coach or consultant | Email list plus one content channel | Trust builds over several touches, and email keeps that relationship going between content pieces |
| Digital product seller | Pinterest or a content channel tied to search | Digital products are usually discovered while someone is researching a problem, not while browsing a feed |

#### What does starting look like in the first thirty days?

It looks smaller than most owners expect. Setting up a Google Business Profile, creating a Pinterest business account and connecting it to your website, or writing the first three emails for a welcome sequence, are each things you can finish inside a single afternoon. The first thirty days are about setup and one steady habit, not about seeing a result yet. Owners who expect a big number in the first month often quit right before the channel would have started working, since most channels take longer than a month to build any real momentum.

#### How much time does marketing actually take each week?

Enough to show up consistently, which matters more than showing up often. A Pinterest account posted to for thirty focused minutes a week, every week, will usually outperform one posted to heavily for two weeks and then abandoned. Pick a pace you can actually keep for six months before you judge whether the channel works.

#### What if you have almost no marketing budget?

Pick the channel with the lowest cost to start, which for most small businesses is Pinterest, email or your Google Business Profile, since all three are free to set up and maintain yourself. [Growing an Email List From Scratch](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/growing-an-email-list-from-scratch) and [Pinterest SEO for Beginners](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/pinterest-seo-beginners-guide) both cover starting points that do not require paid ads.

#### What if you are not sure your website can handle any of these channels yet?

Test it before you invest more time sending traffic to it. Pick your five most important pages, the ones a new customer would land on first, and check that each one loads quickly on a phone, states what you offer and gives a clear next step. A channel cannot fix a website that confuses the very people it sends there. If that check turns up real problems, fixing the website earns you more from every channel you eventually run, since the same visitors will convert at a higher rate without spending anything extra on marketing itself.

#### When should you add a second channel?

Once the first channel is running on its own without daily attention, and you can point to some result from it, even a small one. Adding a second channel before the first is steady usually means neither one gets the attention it needs. [What Is Digital Strategy for a Small Business?](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/what-is-digital-strategy-for-small-business) is a good next read once more than one channel is running, since it walks through how the pieces connect. [The Customer Journey for Service Businesses, Step by Step](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/customer-journey-for-service-businesses) is useful once your first channel starts sending real visitors somewhere. If you would rather see every option side by side with prices, [Marie Glow Studio's full services page](https://marieglowstudio.com/services) lays out web design, Pinterest, SEO and strategy together.

#### Frequently asked questions

**What is the best first marketing channel for a small business?**

There is no single best channel for every business. The right first channel is wherever your specific customers already search or browse, which looks different for a handmade product shop than for a local plumber, so the honest starting point depends on your business type, not a general rule.

**Should I be on every social platform at once?**

No. Spreading limited time and attention across many platforms usually means none of them build enough consistency to actually work, since each one needs a steady rhythm to gain any traction. One channel done consistently for months will usually outperform several platforms posted to occasionally.

**Do I need a website before I start marketing?**

You need somewhere ready for interested people to land and take a clear next step once a channel sends them there. If your website is not ready to receive visitors, or is missing a clear next step, fixing that is the actual first marketing task, even before choosing a channel.

**How long before a marketing channel shows results?**

It varies by channel and by how much consistent effort goes in, but most organic channels, including Pinterest and search, take several months of steady work before results become clear and reliable. Email can show smaller, faster signs of progress once a list starts growing.

**When should a small business add a second marketing channel?**

Once the first channel runs steadily without needing constant daily attention, and you can point to some real result from it, even a small one. Adding a second channel before the first has settled usually means neither channel gets the attention it needs to actually build momentum.

### Why Your Website Is Not on Google, and How to Fix It

URL: https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/why-your-website-is-not-on-google
Topic: SEO and Search Visibility | Published: 2026-09-10

A website usually is not on Google because it has not been indexed yet, a noindex tag or robots.txt file is blocking it, the domain is too new for Google to have crawled it, or the pages are too thin for Google to want to show. Google Search Console will tell you which one it is.

Search Console, Google's free tool for site owners, matters here because guessing wastes time. It shows exactly which pages are indexed, which are not, and the reason for each one. If you have not connected it yet, that is the first step before anything below.

#### Is my website even indexed?

Indexed means Google has crawled the page and added it to the list it can show in search results. A page can exist, look fine and still not be indexed. In Search Console, use the URL Inspection tool on your homepage and a few important pages to see the actual indexing status Google reports, not a guess.

#### Could a noindex tag be blocking my pages?

Yes, and it happens more than owners expect, usually left over from a staging site or a plugin default that was never turned off after launch. A noindex tag tells search engines directly not to show a page. Check your page source or Search Console's page indexing report for pages marked excluded by noindex tag.

#### Could my robots.txt file be the problem?

It could. robots.txt is a small file at yoursite.com/robots.txt that tells search engines which parts of the site they may crawl. A rule left over from development, such as one disallowing the whole site, will keep Google out entirely. Open the file directly in a browser and read it, or check the robots.txt section of Search Console.

- Connect Google Search Console and verify ownership of the domain

- Check the Pages report for indexed versus not indexed counts

- Use URL Inspection on your most important pages to see the specific reason

- Open your robots.txt file directly and read every rule in it

- Check individual pages for a noindex meta tag in the page source

- Submit or resubmit your sitemap through Search Console

#### Is my domain simply too new?

It might be. A brand new domain has no crawl or trust history yet, and Google typically needs some time, often a few weeks, to discover and index a new site even when nothing is technically wrong. Submitting a sitemap through Search Console speeds this up, but there is no way to skip the waiting entirely.

#### Could my pages be too thin to rank?

Yes. A page with a few lines of text and little else gives Google little reason to show it for anything specific. This shows up differently than a hard block: the page may be indexed but never appear for relevant searches. [Answer Engine Optimization for Small Business](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/answer-engine-optimization-for-small-business) covers how to write pages that both Google and AI tools can understand and quote.

| Symptom in Search Console | Likely cause | Where to check |
| Excluded by noindex tag | A leftover noindex tag or plugin setting | Page source, or your CMS's SEO settings |
| Blocked by robots.txt | A disallow rule left in from development | yoursite.com/robots.txt |
| Discovered, currently not indexed | New domain, or a page Google has not prioritized yet | Sitemap submission, and time |
| Indexed but not ranking for relevant terms | Thin content, weak titles or few internal links | The page itself, and your internal linking |

#### What if Search Console shows almost no data at all?

That usually means the property was only just connected, or the domain is genuinely new enough that Google has not crawled much of it yet. Give it a few days after verifying ownership and submitting a sitemap before reading too much into empty reports. If weeks pass with still nothing, double check that the site was verified correctly and that the sitemap URL actually loads without an error.

#### Could a recent redesign or domain change be the cause?

Yes. Moving to a new domain, restructuring page URLs, or relaunching a site without 301 redirects from the old addresses can quietly erase indexing that used to exist. Google treats a changed URL as a new page unless it is told otherwise through a redirect, so old rankings and indexing do not automatically carry over. Anyone who redesigned a site recently should check Search Console for a drop in indexed pages around that date specifically.

#### Does page speed or mobile usability affect indexing?

Speed and mobile usability affect ranking more directly than indexing itself, but a page that fails to load reliably can also fail to crawl properly, which does affect indexing. Check the Core Web Vitals and mobile usability reports in Search Console alongside the pages report, since a slow or broken page can sit indexed and still barely appear for anyone. Once indexing itself is confirmed clean, weak internal linking is often the next thing worth reviewing, since [Local SEO for Service Businesses](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/local-seo-for-service-businesses) covers how linking between a site's own pages helps both indexing and ranking.

#### What should I check first?

Start with Search Console itself, since it tells you which of these problems you actually have instead of guessing. From there, fix a hard block like noindex or robots.txt first, since nothing else matters until Google can even reach the page. Then move to sitemap submission, and finally to page quality, internal links and page speed once the technical door is open.

If the technical basics turn out fine and the real issue is thin, unclear content, the fastest path is often a full [Website SEO Audit](https://marieglowstudio.com/website-seo-audit), which checks indexing, on-page SEO, local SEO and AI search readiness together and hands back a prioritized fix list instead of a pile of separate reports.

#### Frequently asked questions

**How long does it take for Google to index a new website?**

It varies, but many new sites are at least partially indexed within a few days to a few weeks of submitting a sitemap through Google Search Console. A site with no technical blocks and a submitted sitemap usually appears faster than one left to be discovered on its own.

**Does Bing need the same fixes as Google?**

Mostly yes. Indexing, noindex tags, robots.txt rules and thin content affect Bing the same way they affect Google. Bing Webmaster Tools mirrors much of what Search Console offers, and both are worth setting up rather than assuming one search engine covers the other.

**Can a website be indexed but still not show up for my keywords?**

Yes. Being indexed only means Google has the page available to show. Ranking for a specific search depends on content quality, relevance, internal links and competition, which is a separate problem from indexing and needs its own fix.

**Will submitting a sitemap guarantee my pages get indexed?**

No. A sitemap simply tells Google which pages exist and speeds up discovery. Google still decides whether to index and rank each page based on content quality, technical accessibility and how the page compares to others already ranking.

**Should I worry if only some of my pages are indexed?**

Not automatically. Thin pages, duplicate content or pages you deliberately blocked, such as an internal search results page, are often fine to leave out. Check each excluded page in Search Console before assuming it is a problem worth fixing.

### How Much Does a Small Business Website Cost

URL: https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/how-much-does-a-small-business-website-cost
Topic: Shopify and Web Design | Published: 2026-09-06

A small business website can cost anywhere from nothing, on a free platform plan, to several thousand dollars for a custom multi page build, and the real driver of that range is scope rather than the platform, since a simple one page site for a straightforward business costs far less than a multi page store with many products.

Comparing options by price alone misses what each one actually includes. The more useful comparison looks at what is done for you, what you still have to do yourself, and how long it takes.

#### What does a DIY website actually cost?

Little in cash, but real time. Platforms like Shopify, Squarespace or Wix charge a low recurring platform fee, but the owner still has to choose a theme, write every page, pick products or services, set up navigation, test mobile design and troubleshoot anything that breaks. For a business owner who already has the time and enjoys the process, DIY can be the right first step, and plenty of small businesses run for years on a well kept DIY site before outgrowing it.

#### What do templates and themes cost, and what do they skip?

Premium themes usually add a modest one time cost on top of the platform fee. A theme gives structure and design decisions upfront, which saves time, but it does not write your copy, choose your photos or configure the site around your specific services and customers. Someone still has to do that work.

#### What does hiring a freelancer or agency cost?

This varies the most, from a few hundred dollars for a simple one page site to well over ten thousand for a large custom build with e-commerce, integrations and ongoing support. The price mostly tracks scope: number of pages, custom design versus a template, copywriting, product or service setup, and how much back and forth the project needs. A designer working from a clear, published price list, rather than a custom quote for every job, tends to be easier to compare against other options, since the scope behind the number is already spelled out.

#### What actually drives the price up or down?

- Number of pages and how much content each one needs
- Custom design versus a starting theme or template
- Whether copywriting and photography are included or supplied by the owner
- E-commerce complexity: number of products, variants and payment setup
- Booking, quote forms or other custom functionality
- Branding work, such as a logo and style guide, bundled in or handled separately
- Revisions, training and post-launch support

#### What costs get missed when comparing website prices?

Ongoing costs beyond the initial build. A domain name renews yearly, a platform or hosting fee usually recurs monthly, and apps or plugins added later often carry their own small charges. A maintenance plan, if the business wants one, is typically separate from the design price as well. None of these make a website a bad investment, but leaving them out of a budget comparison makes a cheap option look cheaper than it actually is over a full year.

#### What should raise a flag when comparing quotes?

A quote with no written scope, no mention of what happens after launch, or a price that seems far below every other quote for the same list of pages. A written scope should say the platform, the pages, who writes the copy, the number of revisions, the timeline and what support continues after the site goes live. Without that in writing, it is hard to know what the price actually buys.

#### How do the main options compare?

| Option | Typical cost | What you still provide |
| DIY on a platform | A low recurring platform fee only | All design, copy, setup and testing time |
| Premium theme plus DIY setup | Platform fee plus a modest one time theme cost | Copy, photos, product or service setup |
| Freelancer, one page site | A few hundred dollars | Brand assets, copy, photos, if not included |
| Freelancer or small studio, multi page custom build | One thousand or more, scope dependent | Varies by what is included in the quote |
| Larger agency build | Several thousand and up | Least, but at the highest cost |

#### What is one real example of published small business web design pricing?

Marie Glow Studio publishes its own prices rather than quoting case by case. The [Website Starter](https://marieglowstudio.com/website-starter) is a professional one page site, delivered in about five business days, priced at $249 with details listed on [the pricing page](https://marieglowstudio.com/services). The [Complete Website and Brand Identity](https://marieglowstudio.com/complete-website-package), a full brand identity plus a multi page site, is priced at $1,497. Seeing one real, published example makes it easier to judge whether a quote from anyone else is in a reasonable range for the scope described.

#### How do you decide what is worth paying for?

By naming the actual bottleneck. Money, time, confidence with the tools and how much the current site is costing the business in lost bookings or sales are all different bottlenecks, and each one points toward a different answer.

Compare the time you would spend doing it yourself against the price of paying someone else, then weigh that against how much the website's performance actually affects your business. A simple site for a new business with plenty of time may be fine as DIY. A business that is losing bookings or sales to a confusing or dated site may get more value from paying for a proper build. [How Long Does It Take to Build a Website](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/how-long-does-it-take-to-build-a-website) covers the timeline side of that same decision.

For a plain breakdown of every Marie Glow Studio price and what each includes, see [all services and pricing](https://marieglowstudio.com/services).

#### Frequently asked questions

**What is the cheapest way to get a small business website?**

A DIY build on a platform like Shopify, Squarespace or Wix, using the platform's own templates. It costs little in cash but takes real time to set up and maintain.

**Why do website prices vary so much between designers?**

Because scope varies: number of pages, custom design versus a template, whether copy and photography are included, and how much functionality like booking or e-commerce is needed.

**Is a more expensive website always better?**

Not necessarily. A higher price should reflect more scope, more custom work or more included support, not just a bigger number. Compare what is included, not price alone.

**Does website cost include ongoing expenses?**

Often not fully. Domain registration, hosting or platform fees and any maintenance plan are usually separate from a one time design cost, so ask what is and is not included.

### The Customer Journey for Service Businesses, Step by Step

URL: https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/customer-journey-for-service-businesses
Topic: Digital Strategy | Published: 2026-09-02

A service business customer journey runs through six stages: discovery, the service page, trust, an inquiry, a booking and follow up afterward. Most service businesses, from a hair salon to a coaching practice, lose more clients in the gap between discovery and booking than in any other part of the business.

Unlike a product sale, a service sale usually asks someone to trust a person before trusting a result. That changes where the friction shows up, and it changes what fixing the journey actually requires.

#### What are the stages of a service business customer journey?

The stages follow the same order almost every time, whether the business is a spa, a contractor or a one-person coaching practice.

- Discovery, usually through a search, a referral or a Pinterest pin
- The service page, where they check if you do what they need
- Trust, built through reviews, photos of past work, credentials and a clear about page
- An inquiry, through a form, a call or a message
- A booking, confirmed through a scheduling tool or a signed agreement
- Follow up, which decides whether they come back or refer someone else

#### Where do service businesses lose the most clients?

Most often between the service page and the inquiry. A visitor who found the right business still leaves because the page does not say what is included, what it costs, or how long it takes, and asking feels like more effort than it should be. The table below shows the usual drop-off points, why they happen and a plain fix for each.

| Drop off point | Common cause | Fix |
| Service page | No pricing range, no clear list of what is included | State a starting price or range and list what the service covers |
| Trust | No reviews, no photos of real work, generic stock images | Add real reviews and real photos, even a small number |
| Inquiry | A contact form with too many fields, or no form at all | Shorten the form, or add a direct booking link instead |
| Booking | No live availability, replies take days | Connect a booking tool such as Acuity Scheduling, Square Appointments or Calendly so a client can see open times immediately |
| Follow up | No reminder before the appointment, no message after | Automate a confirmation and reminder, and send one short message after the service |

#### What does a mapped journey look like in practice?

Picture a spa that gets steady traffic from a Pinterest pin about a specific facial treatment. A visitor lands on the treatment page, likes what she reads, and looks for a price. There is none listed, only a note to call for details. She does not call. Nothing about the pin, the page or the spa was wrong on its own, but the journey broke at the exact point where a decision needed to happen, and the spa never sees that visitor again to know why.

Mapping the journey means walking through that same path yourself and noticing the moment you would have hesitated, then fixing that one moment before worrying about anything else. For the spa in this example, the fix might be as small as adding a price range and a booking button to the same page, rather than a full website rebuild.

#### How do booking tools fit into the journey?

They sit at the exact point where interest turns into a commitment, so a slow or confusing booking step costs more than a slow homepage does. Tools such as Square Appointments, Acuity Scheduling and Calendly let a visitor see real availability and confirm a time without waiting on a reply. Connecting one of these to your website removes an entire round of back and forth email, which is often the step that loses an otherwise interested client. [Marie Glow Studio's work for service businesses](https://marieglowstudio.com/for-service-businesses) is built around connecting the website to whichever booking or quote tool you already use, rather than replacing it.

#### How do you map your own service business's journey?

Walk it the way a new client would. Search for your own business, land on your service page, try to figure out pricing, then attempt to book an appointment using only what is on the page. Time how long each step takes and note anywhere you had to guess. That walk-through will surface the same friction real clients hit, usually within the first two stages.

#### Does the journey look different for a coach than for a salon?

The stages stay the same, but trust carries more weight for a coach, since the service is less tangible and harder to judge from a photo. A salon can lean on before and after photos of past work. A coach usually needs a clearer explanation of what a session actually includes, real testimonials, and a low friction way to ask a question before committing to a paid call. Both still run through discovery, a service page, trust, an inquiry, a booking and follow up, but the amount of trust building needed before someone will inquire tends to be higher for a service that is harder to see in advance.

#### What should a service business fix first?

Fix whichever stage loses the most people, not whichever stage is easiest to fix. For most service businesses that means the service page and the inquiry step, since those two stages sit right before the moment someone would have paid. [What Is Digital Strategy for a Small Business?](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/what-is-digital-strategy-for-small-business) covers how this journey connects to search, Pinterest and email, and [How to Measure Small Business Marketing](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/how-to-measure-small-business-marketing) covers how to track whether a fix is actually working once it is in place. If you would rather have the full path mapped for you, the [Digital Strategy Roadmap](https://marieglowstudio.com/digital-strategy-roadmap) walks through each stage and hands you a written 90 day plan.

#### Frequently asked questions

**What is a customer journey for a service business?**

It is the full path someone takes from first finding your business to booking a service and, ideally, coming back again later. For most salons, spas, contractors and coaches, that path runs through discovery, the service page, a trust building stage, an inquiry, a confirmed booking and some kind of follow up afterward.

**Do salons and spas need a booking tool?**

Most benefit from one. Tools such as Square Appointments or Acuity Scheduling let clients see real availability and book immediately, instead of waiting hours or days for a reply to a message or a call, which gives an interested client time to book with someone else instead.

**Why do people inquire but never book?**

Usually because the next step after inquiring was unclear or slow. A missing price range, a long intake form, or a delayed reply from the business all give an interested person time to lose momentum, change their mind, or simply book with a competitor whose process felt easier.

**How do reviews affect the service business journey?**

Reviews sit in the trust stage, right before someone is willing to actually inquire. A service page with no reviews, no real photos of past work and only stock imagery asks a visitor to trust a stranger with far less information than they would want before booking or paying.

**Does the customer journey end at booking?**

No. What happens after the service, such as a confirmation message, a reminder before the appointment or a short note afterward, affects whether that client returns or refers someone else. Follow up is part of the journey, not an optional extra step tacked on at the end.

### Google Business Profile Checklist for Small Businesses

URL: https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/google-business-profile-checklist
Topic: SEO and Search Visibility | Published: 2026-08-29

A Google Business Profile checklist covers claiming or verifying the listing, setting an accurate category and service area, filling in hours, photos and a description, then keeping it current with posts and review replies. It is usually the first thing a nearby customer sees, often before your website loads.

Most businesses set this up once, years ago, and never look at it again. Details drift: a phone number changes, hours shift for a season, a category no longer fits. Work through the sections below in order, since each builds on the one before it.

#### How do I claim or verify a Google Business Profile?

Search your business name on Google Maps or Google Search. If a profile already exists, claim it through the prompt on the listing. If nothing comes up, create one directly at google.com/business. Verification usually happens by postcard, phone or video, depending on the business type, and the profile will not show fully in search until it is verified.

#### What category should I choose, and does it matter?

It matters more than most owners expect, because your primary category controls a lot of what Google decides to show for. Choose the most specific accurate category available, such as hair salon rather than beauty salon if that is genuinely the closer match, then add secondary categories for anything else you truly offer.

#### Should a service area business hide its address?

Yes, if there is no public storefront customers walk into. Google Business Profile has a setting for exactly this: mark the business as a service area business, hide the address, and list the cities, counties or zip codes you actually serve. Home services, mobile businesses, contractors and many consultants use this setting.

- Confirm your business name matches your website and other listings exactly

- Set your category, and add any secondary categories that genuinely apply

- Enter your service area, or your public address if customers visit you

- Add your phone number, website link and accurate hours, including holiday hours

- Upload current photos of the location, team, vehicles or finished work

- Write a description in your own words, without keyword stuffing

- Turn on messaging or bookings if you can actually respond to them

#### What details are easy to get wrong?

A handful of small fields cause most of the problems worth checking:

| Field | Common mistake |
