A new list needs a place to collect addresses and a way to greet each new subscriber. [Flodesk](https://flodesk.com/c/MARIEGEMS) is one platform to explore for signup forms and welcome sequences.

#### What is worth reading after this?

[Why Every Small Business Needs an Email List](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/why-every-small-business-needs-an-email-list.html) explains why a list belongs in your marketing mix. To keep new subscribers from slipping away, read [Email Marketing Mistakes Small Businesses Make](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/email-marketing-mistakes-small-businesses-make.html). And if Pinterest is meant to be one of your sources of visitors, the [Pinterest SEO Audit](https://marieglowstudio.com/pinterest-audit.html) looks at how your account is organized as part of its review.

#### Frequently asked questions

**How do I get my first email subscribers?**

Start with existing customers and interested followers, share a useful signup offer, and add it to relevant website pages. Invite people openly, and never add anyone without their consent.

**Should I buy an email list?**

No. Purchased contacts did not request your emails and can damage trust, deliverability, and compliance.

**Is a lead magnet required to get the first subscribers?**

Not always, but a relevant resource or benefit gives people a clearer reason to subscribe than a generic newsletter promise.

### Email Marketing Mistakes Small Businesses Make

URL: https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/email-marketing-mistakes-small-businesses-make
Topic: Email Marketing | Published: 2026-07-24

Permission to email someone is worth protecting. Most email mistakes come from treating a list like a number instead of a group of real people. The biggest ones are emailing people who never agreed, promising something vague at signup, skipping the welcome email, and sending only sales messages.

#### Why does email permission matter so much?

Email marketing gives a small business direct access to people who asked to hear from it, which makes that permission worth protecting. The goal is not to send as often as possible or push a sale in every message. Most of the mistakes below come from unclear expectations or inconsistent systems.

#### Is adding people without clear consent a mistake?

Yes, and it is the most serious one. Do not upload contacts simply because they purchased, messaged, followed, or handed you a business card unless the permission and applicable requirements support marketing email. Sending to people who did not clearly consent can damage trust and deliverability, so build a permission-based list.

#### What is wrong with a vague signup promise?

A vague promise attracts the wrong subscribers. Tell people what they will receive and what future emails may include. A specific benefit earns more qualified subscribers than "join our newsletter."

#### What happens when the lead magnet does not arrive?

The signup feels broken. Send the promised guide, code, template, or confirmation immediately and test the link on mobile.

#### Why is skipping the welcome email a mistake?

A welcome email works best while the signup is still fresh. Introduce the sender, fulfill the promise, set expectations, and give one useful next step. [What Happens After Someone Joins Your Email List?](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/what-happens-after-someone-joins-your-email-list.html) shows what to send and in which order.

#### How do misleading subject lines hurt an email?

They break the promise the subject made. A subject can create curiosity without hiding the truth. The email should deliver what the subject and preview text imply.

#### Should every email be a promotion?

No. Mix offers with education, product guidance, stories, FAQs, resources, and customer support so subscribers have reasons to stay. Constant discounts can also reduce margin and train customers to wait, so use value, access, and relevant offers too.

#### What goes wrong with inconsistent sending?

Subscribers forget why they joined. Choose a realistic schedule. If you return after a long break, briefly remind people who you are and why they subscribed.

#### What does ignoring testing and list health look like?

It looks like broken links, a wrong name in a greeting, an email that is hard to read on a phone, or unsubscribes that keep receiving mail. Check links, personalization, mobile layout, sender information, replies, bounces, unsubscribes, and engagement. Remove or suppress contacts as your platform and legal requirements direct.

#### Which mistakes should you fix first?

If you can only fix a few things this week, work in this order:

- Confirm that everyone on the list agreed to hear from you.
- Rewrite the signup promise so it says what people receive.
- Check that the lead magnet and welcome email send immediately.
- Set a schedule you can keep and tell subscribers what it is.
- Test the whole journey on your phone, from form to inbox.

#### Where can you build a permission-based list?

The Flodesk link below is a referral link. I may earn a commission if you purchase through one of these links, at no additional cost to you.

Several of these fixes depend on how signups are collected and how new subscribers are welcomed, and [Flodesk](https://flodesk.com/c/MARIEGEMS) is worth a look for building the signup form and the welcome automation.

#### What should you read to avoid these email mistakes?

For a compact foundation to build on, read [The 5 Emails Every Small Business Needs](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/five-emails-every-small-business-needs.html). To grow the list the right way from the first subscriber, read [Growing an Email List From Scratch](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/growing-an-email-list-from-scratch.html). If Pinterest is one place your signups come from, the [Pinterest SEO Audit](https://marieglowstudio.com/pinterest-audit.html) is a one-time review with no monthly contract.

#### Frequently asked questions

**What is the biggest email marketing mistake?**

Sending to people who did not clearly consent can damage trust and deliverability. Build a permission-based list.

**Should every email include a discount?**

No. Constant discounts can reduce margin and train customers to wait. Use education, value, access, and relevant offers too.

**Why are welcome emails important?**

They confirm the signup, deliver what was promised, introduce the business, and set expectations while interest is high.

### Welcome Email Sequence Examples for Small Businesses

URL: https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/welcome-email-sequence-examples
Topic: Email Marketing | Published: 2026-07-24

A welcome sequence isn't a complicated funnel. It's a handful of emails that actually deliver what you promised, in the right order. Below are four examples: a three-email lead magnet sequence, a product-business sequence, a service-business sequence, and a waitlist sequence, each showing the purpose of every email.

These examples are frameworks, not scripts to copy without thinking. Adjust the timing, voice, disclosures, products, and calls to action based on what the person signed up to receive.

#### What is a welcome email sequence?

A welcome sequence is simply a planned set of emails that delivers what was promised, introduces the business, helps the subscriber, and offers a relevant next step.

#### What does a three-email lead magnet sequence look like?

- Email one immediately delivers the resource and welcomes the subscriber.
- Email two, one or two days later, helps them use it.
- Email three connects the topic to a relevant product, service, or article.

#### What does a welcome sequence look like for a product business?

- Email one confirms signup or sends the offer.
- Email two explains how to choose or use the product category.
- Email three shares materials, care, or process.
- Email four highlights a collection or customer favorite.
- Email five answers common buying questions.

#### What does a welcome sequence look like for a service business?

- Email one delivers the guide.
- Email two identifies the common problem.
- Email three explains the service process.
- Email four shares a case study or real example.
- Email five invites a consultation or service-page visit.

#### What does a waitlist welcome sequence look like?

- Email one confirms the waitlist and expectations.
- Email two teaches something related to the future offer.
- Email three shares behind-the-scenes progress.
- Email four provides launch timing.
- Email five announces access clearly.

#### How soon should the first welcome email go out?

When someone expects a download, code, or confirmation, send it within minutes. Test the automation and link before promoting the form. [What Happens After Someone Joins Your Email List?](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/what-happens-after-someone-joins-your-email-list.html) describes what should happen around that first message.

#### Why give each email only one purpose?

Choose a main message and primary call to action. Extra links can exist, but the reader should understand the next step.

#### How do you build trust before applying pressure?

Useful guidance, clear expectations, honest proof, and relevant stories make later offers feel connected instead of sudden. [The 5 Emails Every Small Business Needs](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/five-emails-every-small-business-needs.html) describes the five messages most small businesses can start with.

#### What happens when the sequence ends?

After the sequence, add subscribers to the appropriate ongoing segment or newsletter and continue the type of content they expected. A sequence that ends in silence wastes the goodwill it built.

#### What can send a welcome sequence for you?

The Flodesk link below is a referral link. I may earn a commission if you purchase through one of these links, at no additional cost to you.

Because a welcome sequence is a set of automated emails, you need a platform that can send it for you, and [Flodesk](https://flodesk.com/c/MARIEGEMS) is one you can explore for welcome automations and signup forms.

#### What should you read after these sequence examples?

To see how the pieces fit into a full list-building plan, read [Growing an Email List From Scratch](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/growing-an-email-list-from-scratch.html). If your sequence depends on Pinterest visitors joining, the [Pinterest SEO Audit](https://marieglowstudio.com/pinterest-audit.html) is delivered as a single document within 4 business days of purchase.

#### Frequently asked questions

**How many emails should a welcome sequence include?**

Three to five emails are enough for many small businesses, though the right length depends on the promise, audience, and offer.

**How far apart should welcome emails be?**

Send delivery immediately, then space later emails roughly one to three days apart as a starting point. Adjust based on content and engagement.

**What should the first welcome email say?**

Thank the subscriber, deliver the promised item, briefly introduce the sender, set expectations, and provide one clear next step.

**Should a welcome sequence include a sales email?**

It can include a relevant offer after delivering value and context. The offer should match the reason the person subscribed.

### Managing Overwhelm as a Small Business Owner

URL: https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/managing-overwhelm-as-a-small-business-owner
Topic: Behind the Brand | Published: 2026-07-24

Quick answer: Manage small-business overwhelm by narrowing priorities, using simple systems, setting boundaries, and planning realistic work.

Small-business overwhelm doesn't always mean you're doing something wrong. It usually means one person is carrying product creation, customer service, marketing, bookkeeping, and every decision in between, alone.

I do not believe the answer is pretending we can perfectly balance everything. The goal is to notice what is creating pressure and make the next step smaller and clearer.

#### Get every task out of your head

Use one trusted list for active tasks, deadlines, waiting items, and ideas. Your brain should not have to keep repeating reminders all day.

#### Choose the real priority

Ask what must happen today, what meaningfully moves the business forward, and what can wait. A long list is not a plan until it has an order.

#### Work in smaller batches

Group similar work such as product photos, listings, emails, Pins, packing, or bookkeeping. Switching less often can reduce the mental weight of starting over.

#### Define a good-enough version

Not every graphic, email, or page needs to become the final masterpiece. Decide what accurate, useful, and on-brand looks like, then finish that version.

#### Create simple repeatable systems

Templates, checklists, saved replies, naming rules, and weekly routines reduce the number of decisions required for work you do repeatedly.

#### Set customer boundaries clearly

Publish turnaround times, business hours, revision limits, and communication expectations. Boundaries protect both the owner and the customer from confusion.

#### Plan around real life

Build schedules around the responsibilities and energy you actually have. A realistic plan that gets completed is better than an ideal plan that creates guilt.

#### Recognize when rest is the next task

Rest can prevent rushed errors, resentment, and burnout. If everything feels urgent and nothing is getting clearer, stepping away may be the most productive choice.

#### Frequently asked questions

**Why do small-business owners feel overwhelmed?**

Owners often handle many roles with limited time, money, and support. Constant decisions, unclear priorities, and pressure to be visible everywhere add to the load.

**How can I reduce business overwhelm today?**

Write every task down, choose one essential outcome, break it into the smallest next action, and move nonessential work to a later list.

**Is it okay to pause marketing?**

A short planned pause may be healthier than continuing at an unsustainable pace. Keep essential customer communication active and return with a simpler schedule.

**When is overwhelm becoming burnout?**

Ongoing exhaustion, detachment, irritability, loss of motivation, and difficulty recovering may signal burnout. Consider reducing demands and seeking appropriate professional support.

### Why Progress Matters More Than Perfection

URL: https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/why-progress-matters-more-than-perfection
Topic: Behind the Brand | Published: 2026-07-24

Quick answer: Learn why progress matters more than perfection when building a small business and how small completed steps create feedback and confidence.

A business can't learn from work that stays hidden forever. Perfection just means the feedback never arrives.

But a business cannot learn from work that stays hidden forever. Progress creates information. It shows what customers understand, what they ask for, and what needs to improve next.

#### Finished work creates feedback

A published page, tested product, sent email, or completed Pin gives you real information. Private polishing only gives you more opinions inside your own head.

#### Small steps build confidence

Confidence often follows action rather than arriving before it. Completing manageable tasks proves that you can move through uncertainty.

#### Perfect is not a fixed target

Your skills, audience, products, and brand will change. What feels final today may need an update later, so waiting for permanent perfection is unrealistic.

#### Define what ready means

Set practical standards: accurate, safe, on-brand, functional, proofread, tested, and useful. Ready does not mean careless.

#### Separate improvement from avoidance

Ask whether another revision will meaningfully help the customer or whether it is delaying the discomfort of publishing.

#### Create versions and review dates

Launch the best responsible version you can, then schedule a review after real use. This makes improvement part of the process instead of a condition for starting.

#### Notice the small wins

Track finished listings, customer replies, fixed links, learned tools, packed orders, published articles, and consistent weeks. Growth is often built from ordinary completed work.

#### Rest is part of progress

Sustainable progress includes recovery. Exhaustion does not make work more valuable, and a pause does not erase what you have built.

#### Frequently asked questions

**Does progress over perfection mean lowering quality?**

No. It means meeting responsible standards and completing useful work without demanding an impossible final version.

**How do I know when something is ready to publish?**

Check accuracy, functionality, customer clarity, brand fit, safety, links, mobile display, and proofreading. If those essentials are met, publish and learn.

**What if I make a mistake after launching?**

Correct it honestly and improve the process. Most small-business work can be updated, and customers value clear communication.

**How can I stop overediting?**

Set a deadline, a review checklist, and a maximum number of revision rounds before publishing.

### Small Wins That Help Grow a Business

URL: https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/small-wins-that-help-grow-a-business
Topic: Behind the Brand | Published: 2026-07-24

Quick answer: Recognize small business wins that build sustainable growth, including completed listings, better systems, customer feedback, and consistent content.

Growth gets described through viral posts and sold-out launches. Most of it actually happens in the quieter work nobody posts about.

A fixed link, finished description, packed order, customer reply, saved template, or consistent week can make the next month easier. Small wins compound when we notice and build on them.

#### Finishing one important task

Completing the product listing, sending the proposal, publishing the page, or testing the form creates movement that an endless task list cannot.

#### Improving one repeatable system

A packing checklist, email template, file naming rule, pricing sheet, content calendar, or saved reply reduces future effort.

#### Answering a customer question clearly

Every real question can improve a product description, FAQ, policy, email, or service page for the next person.

#### Showing up consistently at a realistic pace

A manageable routine builds a useful library over time. Consistency does not require being visible on every platform every day.

#### Learning what not to continue

Stopping an unprofitable product, unused tool, weak offer, or exhausting process can create space for stronger work.

#### Making the website easier to use

Fixing navigation, a broken button, missing policy, unclear headline, or mobile overlap can quietly improve every future visit.

#### Protecting profit and time

Updating a price, setting a boundary, batching work, or declining the wrong project supports a more sustainable business.

#### Recording progress

Keep a simple monthly record of completed work, customer feedback, traffic, orders, email growth, and lessons. Comparison becomes more honest when the starting point is documented.

#### Frequently asked questions

**What counts as a small-business win?**

Any completed action that improves customer experience, revenue potential, clarity, systems, skills, visibility, or sustainability can count.

**Why track small wins?**

Tracking makes progress visible, supports better planning, and prevents large goals from hiding meaningful work.

**Can small tasks really grow revenue?**

Individually they may be modest, but clearer pages, better follow-up, consistent marketing, accurate pricing, and repeatable systems work together.

**How often should progress be reviewed?**

A short weekly review and a more detailed monthly review can reveal patterns without turning tracking into another full-time task.

### I Almost Scrolled Past One Facebook Post… and I'm Glad I Didn't

URL: https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/i-almost-scrolled-past-one-facebook-post
Topic: Behind the Brand | Published: 2026-07-19

#### Quick Answer

Sometimes the opportunities that move your business forward don't come from a huge marketing campaign. They come from one small decision.

For me, it was simply choosing not to keep scrolling.

#### Running a Small Business Means Wearing Every Hat

If you're a small business owner, you probably know this feeling.

You're trying to:

- Create products
- Answer customer emails
- Update your website
- Learn SEO
- Figure out Google
- Post on social media
- Create Pinterest content
- Keep up with AI
- And somehow still run your business.

Some days it feels like you're throwing everything at the wall hoping something sticks.

That was me.

#### The Facebook Post I Almost Ignored

Yesterday, while scrolling through the Wichita Small Business Facebook group, I noticed a post looking for local businesses to join a brand-new Wichita business directory.

I almost kept scrolling.

Then I stopped.

I remember thinking:

"Wait a minute... being listed in a local business directory really isn't a bad thing."

Interestingly, my first thought wasn't getting customers.

It was...

A backlink.

So I scrolled back up and left a comment.

I had no idea that one comment would completely change what I'd spend the next 24 hours working on.

#### What Is a Backlink?

If you've never heard the term before, don't worry.

A backlink is simply another website linking back to yours.

Think of it like another business saying:

"Hey... this business is worth checking out."

Search engines use backlinks as one of many signals when understanding how trustworthy and relevant a website is.

Not every backlink carries the same value, but quality backlinks from reputable, relevant websites can strengthen your online presence over time.

As someone who spends a lot of time learning SEO, I immediately recognized the opportunity.

#### An Unexpected Website Audit

After I commented, the owner of The 316 Directory took the time to give my website a mini audit.

I'll be honest...

It completely made my day.

He complimented:

- My purple branding
- The [Marie Gems](https://mariegems.com) identity
- My website layout
- How clearly my services were explained
- The overall organization of my site

After spending countless hours building my website, hearing that from someone outside my own circle was incredibly encouraging.

But then he pointed out something I hadn't been giving enough attention.

#### My Google Business Profile

While my website looked solid, he explained that improving my Google Business Profile and collecting more Google reviews could significantly strengthen my local SEO.

If SEO sounds intimidating...

It simply means:

Helping search engines understand what your business does so they know when to recommend it.

Then he mentioned something I'd heard before...

Answer Engine Optimization (AEO).

That conversation completely shifted how I think about marketing.

#### Wait... AI Can Recommend Local Businesses?

This was probably the biggest lightbulb moment.

He shared a story about his wife using ChatGPT while asking questions about remodeling a kitchen.

She wasn't searching for a contractor.

She was simply asking questions.

During the conversation, ChatGPT recommended a local remodeling company.

That really made me stop and think.

People aren't only searching Google anymore.

They're asking:

- ChatGPT
- Gemini
- Claude
- Microsoft Copilot

So I started asking myself:

How can I make Marie Gems easier for AI to understand?

That single conversation completely changed the way I looked at my own website.

#### I'm Self-Taught… and I Love Learning

One thing I shared during our conversation is that I'm completely self-taught when it comes to:

- SEO
- Pinterest marketing
- Website optimization
- Most of my digital marketing

I've spent years:

- Reading articles
- Watching videos
- Testing ideas
- Breaking things
- Fixing them
- Learning through trial and error

Because of that, I usually manage my own:

- Website
- SEO
- Google Business Profile
- Pinterest strategy

But I also told him something else.

I'd genuinely enjoy sitting down with someone who sees things differently.

Because no matter how much you know...

Someone else always knows something you don't.

And I never want to stop learning.

#### One Conversation Became Immediate Action

Instead of thinking:

"I should probably do that someday..."

I actually started making changes.

Within the next day I:

- Improved my Google Business Profile
- Built a Shopify AI Knowledge Base
- Added dozens of AI-friendly FAQs
- Learned more about Answer Engine Optimization (AEO)
- Started asking customers for Google reviews

Then I realized something.

I'd had my Google Business Profile for years...

But I had almost never asked customers to leave reviews.

So I opened Flodesk, the email marketing platform I use, and sent an email asking past customers if they'd be willing to leave an honest review.

The responses started coming in.

One after another.

Some honestly brought tears to my eyes.

#### Everything Happened in About 24 Hours

Sometimes it's amazing how quickly momentum builds.

Within one day I:

- Joined The 316 Directory
- Became a Founding Member
- Learned more about AEO
- Improved my Google Business Profile
- Asked customers for reviews
- Built a Shopify AI Knowledge Base
- Added AI-friendly FAQs across my website
- Received multiple new Google reviews

And then...

Marie Gems was officially featured by The 316 Directory.

[https://the316directory.com/blogs/blogs-detail/marie-gems-joins-the-316-directory-as-a-founding-member](https://the316directory.com/blogs/blogs-detail/marie-gems-joins-the-316-directory-as-a-founding-member)

#### Most Business Growth Isn't Exciting

We often imagine success looks like:

- Landing a huge client
- Going viral
- Making thousands overnight

But most real business growth looks much smaller.

It looks like:

- Stopping your scroll.
- Leaving one comment.
- Sending one email.
- Asking for one review.
- Writing one blog post.
- Creating one Pinterest pin.
- Improving one page on your website.

### Shopify SEO for Small Businesses: 15 Easy Ways to Get More Organic Traffic

URL: https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/shopify-seo-for-small-businesses
Topic: Shopify and Web Design | Published: 2026-07-07

I used to hear 'keywords' and 'metadata' and want to close the tab. I made almost every SEO mistake on this list myself. Here's what actually fixed it, one small step at a time. Shopify SEO helps search engines understand your products, collections, pages and blog posts so the right shoppers can find your store.

If you have built a Shopify store but are not getting consistent visitors from Google, you are not alone. Many small business owners focus on creating products and overlook search engine optimization. I understand, because I used to avoid SEO whenever I could.

When I first started my Shopify business, I spent hours creating products and almost no time helping people find them. Eventually I realized that even the most beautiful online store cannot make sales if nobody can find it. Once I stopped trying to master SEO overnight and focused on one small improvement at a time, my products became easier to discover, my blog started bringing in visitors, and SEO became one of my favorite parts of growing my business. If you are still early in building yours, you may also like my guide on [how to start a product-based business from home](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/how-to-start-a-product-based-business-from-home.html).

#### What is Shopify SEO and why does it matter for small businesses?

Shopify SEO is the process of optimizing your online store so search engines can understand your content and match it with people searching for your products or services. It matters because a store that cannot be found cannot sell.

SEO is not about tricking Google. It is about making your website easier for both search engines and real people to understand. That shift made it much less intimidating for me. Instead of chasing algorithms, I ask one question: Would this page genuinely help someone searching for this?

#### What are the 15 easy ways to improve Shopify SEO?

Every step below comes from this guide. The sections that follow explain the product page, collection page, meta, image and internal linking steps in more detail.

- Review your current Shopify traffic sources.
- Find which pages already get visits.
- Choose one product, collection or blog post to improve first.
- Write a unique description for every product instead of pasting short ones.
- Use descriptive headings and answer customer questions on product pages.
- Include relevant keywords naturally.
- Add a helpful description to each collection page.
- Organize products into collections in a logical way.
- Write a clear meta title for every important page.
- Write a meta description that earns the click.
- Give product images descriptive filenames and compress them.
- Write meaningful alt text.
- Link related pages to each other.
- Publish blog posts that answer customer questions.
- Fix the common mistakes below: duplicate content, keyword stuffing, broken links and outdated pages.

#### How does Shopify SEO bring in more organic traffic?

Strong SEO improves visibility, attracts visitors with buying intent and builds long-term traffic without relying entirely on paid advertising. It also takes patience. I used to check my analytics every day hoping for a spike, and most days nothing happened.

Unlike social media, where a post can disappear quickly, a well-optimized product page or blog post can keep bringing visitors for months or even years. Google is one search engine, and Pinterest works as another that can keep sending visitors to your site. If you are ready to expand beyond Google, see [Pinterest SEO strategy](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/pinterest-seo-strategy.html).

To begin, review your traffic sources, note which pages already get visits and pick one product, collection or blog post to improve first.

#### How do you optimize Shopify product pages for SEO?

Write a unique description for each product, use descriptive headings, answer customer questions and include relevant keywords naturally. One of my biggest mistakes was pasting in short descriptions that told shoppers almost nothing, did not answer questions and gave Google very little to work with.

Now I treat every product page like its own small sales page. I explain who the product is for, what makes it useful and why someone would want it. The full method is in [how to create product listings that convert](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/how-to-create-product-listings-that-convert.html).

#### How do you improve Shopify collection pages?

Collection pages are often overlooked, but they can be strong SEO pages. Add a useful collection description, organize products logically and help shoppers see quickly what they will find.

For the longest time I ignored mine. They were simply a grid of products with no description at all. Once I added helpful introductions with the right keywords, those pages became more useful to both visitors and search engines.

#### How do you write SEO-friendly meta titles and descriptions?

Every important Shopify page should have a meta title and meta description that accurately reflect the content and encourage a click. I used to skip meta descriptions because I assumed nobody read them.

Then I realized they are often the first thing someone sees in Google search results. A good meta description does not just help SEO. It helps convince someone to click on your store instead of someone else's.

#### How do you optimize images for Shopify SEO?

Use descriptive filenames, compress images so pages load faster and write meaningful alt text that helps accessibility while supporting your SEO. I learned this one the hard way: my images had filenames like IMG_4839.jpg, which tells Google nothing. Now every product image gets a descriptive filename and alt text before I upload it.

#### How does internal linking help Shopify SEO?

Internal links connect related pages on your site. They help visitors keep learning and help search engines understand how your content is organized.

Once I started blogging consistently, I saw how many chances I had to connect pages. If I am writing about Shopify SEO, it makes sense to link to helpful resources, related blog posts and service pages where readers can take the next step, like the [Shopify store optimization checklist](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/shopify-store-optimization-checklist.html). If you would rather have help, the [Complete Website and Brand Identity](https://marieglowstudio.com/complete-website-package) at Marie Glow Studio includes full Shopify setup, navigation and up to 20 products uploaded and organized with basic SEO. The full range is on the [Shopify web design](https://marieglowstudio.com/web-design.html) page.

#### What Shopify SEO mistakes should you avoid?

The most common are duplicate content, keyword stuffing, missing alt text, broken links, outdated pages and product descriptions that are too short. I made almost every one: I skipped alt text, ignored collection descriptions, reused product descriptions and had pages with almost no content.

The good news is that none of those mistakes permanently ruined my business. I fixed them one step at a time, and you can too.

#### Where should you start with Shopify SEO?

Start with one small task this week. SEO is not something you finish. It is something you improve a little every week, and small improvements add up over time to more traffic, more visibility and more chances for customers to discover your business.

You do not have to become an SEO expert overnight. Update one product description, add alt text to a few images, improve one collection description or write a better meta title. Then choose another next week.

If you are improving your store yourself, browse my curated [Web Designer’s Must-Haves](https://benable.com/mariegems/web-designer-s-must-haves) for useful design resources and workspace ideas.

This post may contain affiliate links. I may earn a commission if you purchase through one of these links, at no additional cost to you.

#### Frequently asked questions

**How long does Shopify SEO take?**

SEO improvements usually take several weeks to several months depending on your niche, competition, and how consistently you optimize your website.

**Do I need a blog for Shopify SEO?**

A blog helps you target additional keywords, answer customer questions, and build more opportunities for people to discover your Shopify store through search.

**Can beginners do Shopify SEO?**

Yes. Many Shopify SEO improvements, such as optimizing titles, descriptions, headings, images, and internal links, can be done without advanced technical knowledge.

### Why Every Small Business Needs an Email List for Growth

URL: https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/why-every-small-business-needs-an-email-list
Topic: Email Marketing | Published: 2026-06-30

One day a post gets attention. The next day it feels like your reach disappeared for no reason. An email list is the one channel a platform update can't take away from you. In practice, a list is a direct line to people who asked to hear from you, not to whoever an algorithm chooses to show.

#### Does email replace social media, Pinterest, or your website?

Email does not replace your website, blog, Pinterest, or social media. It supports them. For example, a blog post can help people find you through search, a Pinterest pin can send new traffic to your website, and your email list can help you keep building the relationship after someone leaves your site.

That makes email one of the small business growth strategies that does not depend on one algorithm. If you are working on visibility first, this guide on [how to create Pinterest pins that get clicks](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/how-to-design-pinterest-pins.html) is a helpful next step because Pinterest and email can work beautifully together, and [How Pinterest and Email Marketing Work Together](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/pinterest-and-email-marketing.html) shows the whole path from a pin to a subscriber.

#### What is a small business email list?

A small business email list is a group of people who have chosen to receive emails from your business. They might sign up through your website, blog, checkout page, lead magnet, pop-up form, or free resource.

These people are called subscribers. They have given you permission to email them because they are interested in your products, services, tips, resources, story, or business updates.

A simple email list usually includes:

- A signup form where people can join.
- A reason to subscribe, such as a discount, checklist, guide, freebie, or helpful resource.
- A welcome email that introduces your business.
- Ongoing emails, such as newsletters, product updates, blog posts, tips, or promotions.

You do not need a huge list to start. A small, engaged list can be more valuable than a large audience that never opens, clicks, or connects. The goal is not to collect random emails. The goal is to build a helpful, trust-based connection with people who are a good fit for your business.

#### Why does an email list matter more than followers?

Social media can be helpful, but it is not something you fully control. Your reach can change. Platforms can shift. Algorithms can make it harder for your content to show up. Accounts can get restricted, hacked, or buried without much warning.

Your email list gives you a more stable marketing foundation because you are building a direct connection with your audience. You still need to respect your subscribers, send helpful content, and follow email marketing rules, but you are not depending only on a platform to decide who sees your message. Instead of only hoping a platform shows your post to the right audience, you can send helpful updates, resources, product news, and reminders straight to your subscribers.

For small business owners, that matters because your email list can help you:

- Share new blog posts with people who already care about your topic.
- Announce product launches, restocks, and seasonal collections.
- Promote services in a softer, more educational way.
- Build trust before someone is ready to buy.
- Stay connected with past customers.
- Invite people back to your website instead of only keeping them on social media.

This is especially helpful if you are growing a product-based business, a Shopify store, or a service-based brand. You can use your blog and [Pinterest marketing](https://marieglowstudio.com/pinterest-marketing.html) to bring people in, then use email to keep the conversation going. Email marketing also makes it easier to share timely updates in a way that feels personal instead of pushy.

Social media helps people discover you. Email helps you stay connected.

#### What can you send to your email list?

One of the biggest reasons business owners put off email marketing is because they are not sure what to send. The good news is your emails do not have to be complicated. You can send:

- A welcome email that introduces who you are and how you help.
- Helpful tips related to your products, services, or niche.
- New blog posts or educational guides.
- Behind-the-scenes updates from your business.
- Product launches, restocks, or seasonal offers.
- Customer stories, testimonials, or before-and-after examples.
- Personal notes that help your audience feel connected to the person behind the business.
- Simple reminders about resources, services, or products you already offer.

For example, if you sell custom products, you might send an email with gift ideas, product care tips, a holiday ordering reminder, or a behind-the-scenes look at how you create designs. If you offer services, you might send a helpful checklist, a short strategy tip, or a blog post that answers a common client question.

#### How do you start an email list without overcomplicating it?

You do not need a perfect funnel, a giant freebie, or a complicated automation setup to start. A simple email list can begin with a few basic pieces.

The Flodesk link below is a referral link. I may earn a commission if you purchase through one of these links, at no additional cost to you.

- Choose an email marketing platform. Look for something beginner-friendly that lets you create signup forms, send newsletters, and set up a simple welcome email.
- Create one signup form. Start with a form for your website, blog, or homepage.
- Give people a clear reason to subscribe. This could be a discount, a checklist, a guide, updates, or helpful tips.
- Write one welcome email. Tell subscribers who you are, what to expect, and where to go next.
- Add your signup form to important pages. Place it on your homepage, blog posts, footer, and any page where new visitors might want to stay connected.

For beginners, [Flodesk](https://flodesk.com/c/MARIEGEMS) can be a helpful place to start because it is designed for beautiful signup forms, newsletters, and simple email workflows without making the process feel overly technical. You can also explore Shopify's email marketing resources if you want to compare how email fits into your ecommerce setup. For what a new subscriber should receive first, see [Welcome Email Sequence Examples for Small Businesses](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/welcome-email-sequence-examples.html).

If your website does not have a clear place for email signups yet, that is also something to think about when reviewing your overall website strategy. The [Shopify web design](https://marieglowstudio.com/web-design.html) page describes how Marie Glow Studio builds personalized Shopify sites around what your customers search for, so visitors can navigate, shop, and sign up with less effort.

#### Which lead magnet ideas work for a small business?

A lead magnet is a free resource or incentive someone receives after joining your email list. It gives people a reason to subscribe beyond "join my newsletter." Your lead magnet does not have to be big. It just needs to be useful and connected to what your audience cares about. Here are a few simple ideas:

- A product care guide.
- A first-order discount code.
- A printable checklist.
- A small business resource list.
- A style guide or gift guide.
- A free mini training.
- A seasonal shopping guide.
- A website or branding checklist.
- A Pinterest content checklist.

The best lead magnet is one that connects naturally to the next step. If someone downloads a product care guide, they may be interested in your products. If someone downloads a Pinterest checklist, they may eventually want help with Pinterest strategy. Keep it simple, useful, and aligned with what you already offer. More options for shops that sell physical goods are in [Lead Magnet Ideas for Product-Based Businesses](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/lead-magnet-ideas-for-product-based-businesses.html).

#### Where should the signup form go on your website?

Once you create a signup form, do not hide it on one random page. Make it easy for interested visitors to find. Good places to add an email signup form include:

- Your homepage.
- Your blog posts.
- Your website footer.
- Your product pages.
- Your service pages.
- Your contact page.
- A dedicated free resource or lead magnet page.

Your blog can be one of the best places to grow your email list because readers are already learning from you. For example, a reader of a business tips post may be interested in a free business checklist, while a reader of a product photography post may want product listing or photography resources. If you are starting with no audience at all, [Growing an Email List From Scratch](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/growing-an-email-list-from-scratch.html) gives the order to build things in.

#### What mistakes slow down a new email list?

Starting an email list is simple, but there are a few mistakes that can make it harder than it needs to be:

- Waiting until your business feels "big enough" to start.
- Only emailing when you are selling something.
- Making your signup form hard to find.
- Promising a freebie but not delivering it clearly.
- Sending emails without a welcome message.
- Trying to build a complicated funnel before you have the basics.
- Buying email lists or emailing people who did not choose to subscribe.

The biggest thing to remember is that email marketing should feel like a relationship, not a constant sales pitch. Teach, help, share, invite, and make it easy for people to take the next step when they are ready. [Email Marketing Mistakes Small Businesses Make](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/email-marketing-mistakes-small-businesses-make.html) goes deeper into each of these.

#### How does an email list support long-term stability?

A small business email list is not just another marketing task. It is a way to build a more stable connection with your audience, especially when social media feels unpredictable. It gives you a channel you can own, nurture, and use again and again.

Start simple. Create one form, write one welcome email, give people one helpful reason to subscribe, and place the signup form where your website visitors can easily find it.

If you want more people to find your blog, lead magnet, or email signup, consider Pinterest. It can help bring long-term traffic to your website, while email helps you continue building trust after someone discovers you. If Pinterest is meant to send people to your signup page, the [Pinterest SEO Audit](https://marieglowstudio.com/pinterest-audit.html) includes a check of how your account connects to your website.

If you want to create forms, welcome sequences, newsletters, and sales emails in one place, explore [Flodesk](https://flodesk.com/c/MARIEGEMS) and choose the features that fit your business.

#### Frequently asked questions

**Do I need an email list if I already have social media?**

Yes, an email list is still helpful even if you are active on social media. Social media helps people discover you, but email helps you stay connected with people who have already shown interest in your business.

**What should I send first?**

Start with a welcome email. Thank the subscriber for joining, introduce your business, explain what they can expect, and share one helpful link or next step.

**How often should a small business email its list?**

Start with a realistic schedule you can maintain. For many small businesses, one or two emails per month is a manageable starting point. Consistency matters more than sending constantly.

**Do I need a lead magnet to start an email list?**

You do not have to have one, but a simple lead magnet can help people understand the value of joining your list. A checklist, guide, discount, or resource list can be enough to start.

### How to Create Product Listings That Convert

URL: https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/how-to-create-product-listings-that-convert
Topic: Shopify and Web Design | Published: 2026-06-29

A product page has to do a job a vendor-table conversation used to do: explain what it is, who it's for, and why someone should trust it, all without a real person there to answer questions. A product listing that converts says what the item is, who it is for, what is included and why ordering feels safe.

If you have ever made a product, taken photos, written a quick description and then wondered why people look but do not buy, the fix usually starts with clarity. A listing needs more than a pretty photo and a price. It also supports Shopify SEO, Pinterest traffic, Google search visibility and the overall shopping experience, so this guide covers how to write listings that convert without sounding robotic, pushy or overly complicated.

#### Why do product listings matter more than most sellers realize?

A product listing is one of the most important parts of an online store because it helps customers decide whether the product is right for them. A strong listing answers questions like these:

- What exactly is this product?
- Who is it made for?
- What problem does it solve, or what feeling does it create?
- What options, sizes, colors or personalization details are available?
- What does the customer need to know before buying?
- Why should they trust this product and this business?

When a page feels unclear, customers hesitate, and hesitating shoppers may leave even if they liked the product at first. This matters most for handmade sellers, Shopify store owners and small product businesses, because customers cannot touch, hold or try the product before buying. Your photos, title, description, details and links have to do that work for them.

#### What does your customer need to know first?

Start with the buyer, not the seller. Many listings fall flat because they open with what the seller wants to say instead of what the buyer needs to understand. Before you write the title, description or SEO fields, ask yourself:

- What would someone need to know before feeling comfortable buying this?
- What would they ask if they were standing in front of me at a vendor event?
- What details could cause confusion if I leave them out?
- What makes this product useful, meaningful, funny, stylish, personal or giftable?
- What does it help the customer do, feel, express, organize, celebrate or remember?

For a custom tumbler, the customer may want to know whether it can include a name, business logo, color theme, photo or quote. For apparel, they may want the printing method, available options, fit expectations and care instructions. Once you know the answers, the copy gets easier to write, because you are helping the customer understand the product instead of forcing a sales pitch.

#### How do you write a clear, searchable product title?

A good title tells shoppers and search engines what the product actually is, while keeping some personality. A vague title like "Sweet Dreams Design" becomes clearer as "Personalized Floral Tumbler With Name" or "Book Lover Graphic Tee for Cozy Readers." A good title can include:

- The product type, such as tumbler, shirt, mug, sticker, transfer, bookmark or digital download
- The audience, such as moms, teachers, nurses, book lovers, bakers or small business owners
- The style or theme, such as floral, funny, cozy, faith-based, minimalist or vintage
- The use case, such as birthday gift, business branding, team event or holiday gift

Shopify's SEO guidance recommends readable, natural keywords in page titles, meta descriptions, alt tags and body content. The word that matters is readable: write titles that make sense to real people, not keyword-stuffed strings.

#### Why should you sell the benefit before the feature?

Features are the basic facts, and benefits explain why the customer should care. You do not hide the details. You explain them in a way that connects to the customer's real life.

Feature-only copy compared with benefit-focused copy
| Feature only | Benefit focused |
| 20 oz tumbler | A 20 oz tumbler that helps keep your favorite drink close during busy workdays, school drop-offs, errands or late-night creative sessions. |
| Custom name design | Add a name or personal detail so the design feels made just for the person receiving it. |
| DTF printed shirt | A wearable design that lets customers show off their humor, hobby, business or personality in everyday life. |
| Sticker sheet | A simple way to personalize packaging, planners, laptops, journals or small business orders. |

People are not just buying a tumbler, shirt or sticker. They are buying something that helps them express a personality, celebrate someone, organize their business or gift thoughtfully.

#### Which product photos remove hesitation?

Photos that show the product clearly, in use and up close remove the most hesitation, because they build trust before a customer reads a sentence. For most listings, try to include:

- A clear main product photo
- A lifestyle photo that shows how the product fits into real life
- A detail photo that shows texture, design, personalization or print quality
- A scale or context photo when size might be unclear
- A variation photo if different options are available
- A branded graphic or information image if customers need instructions

The goal is not to look like a huge brand. It is to make the product feel clear, honest and easy to understand. For lighting, backgrounds and consistency, read [Product Photography Tips That Help Increase Sales](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/product-photography-tips-that-help-increase-sales.html).

#### Which trust-building details belong on a listing?

Any detail a customer would otherwise have to message you to ask about. If they have to write for basic information, the listing probably needs more clarity. Depending on the product, include:

- Available sizes, colors and design options
- Materials or product base information
- Personalization instructions, and how to submit names, photos, logos or design ideas
- Turnaround time, shipping expectations and return or cancellation notes
- Care instructions
- What is included, what is not included and any limitations

The most important rule is accuracy. Do not invent details just to make a listing feel complete. If a shirt brand, color, size or material depends on inventory, use neutral wording so customers know what to expect. A listing can be warm and friendly and still professional.

#### How do you optimize a product listing for Shopify SEO?

Make the page helpful to people first, then optimize the fields search engines read. For Shopify product listing SEO, focus on the product title, description, SEO title, meta description, URL handle, image file names, image alt text, collection placement and internal links from related products, collections and blog posts.

Use your main keyword naturally, without repeating it until the listing is uncomfortable to read. Your theme or apps may already handle some structured product information, but it is still worth making sure your details are accurate, your images are descriptive and the page clearly matches what the product is. For a wider set of steps, see [Shopify SEO for small businesses](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/shopify-seo-for-small-businesses.html).

#### How do internal links and a clear next step help?

They keep a product page from being a dead end. Internal links help customers keep exploring your store and connect related content across your site. From a listing, you can link to related collections, matching products, helpful blog posts, care instruction pages, custom order information and a contact page when customers need custom help.

Pinterest pins often drive traffic to product pages, blog posts and collections, and a great pin can earn the click, but the product page still has to build enough trust to support the sale. If you are designing pins, see [how to design Pinterest pins](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/how-to-design-pinterest-pins.html).

#### What product listing mistakes should you avoid?

A few mistakes are worth watching for, including descriptions that are too short and titles that are cute but not searchable. Others to check:

- Forgetting product benefits: details matter, but benefits show why they matter.
- Blurry or inconsistent photos: photos should reduce hesitation, not create more questions.
- Leaving out personalization instructions: if a customer must submit a name, logo, photo or idea, explain exactly how.
- Keyword stuffing: searchable does not mean repeating the same phrase.
- Burying important information: sizing, turnaround time, care instructions and custom order notes should be easy to find.
- Forgetting the next step: tell shoppers whether to add to cart, choose options, submit personalization, read a guide or contact you.

Many sellers think that selling more means adding more words, but the real fix is usually clearer structure and more useful product details.

#### Is there a simple product listing formula you can reuse?

Yes. When you are not sure where to start, work down this order:

- Customer-focused opening: the feeling, problem, occasion, personality or use case.
- Product explanation: what the item is.
- Design or style details: the look, message or meaning behind the product.
- Benefits: how the product fits into real life.
- Product details: accurate sizing, options, materials, personalization notes and care information.
- Gift or use ideas: relevant occasions or audiences.
- Trust builders: processing notes, FAQs, photo clarity, reviews or policies when relevant.
- Call to action: a clear next step.

This keeps the listing organized while leaving room to sound human. The best descriptions do not read as if they were copied from a supplier. They read as if a real business owner who understands the customer wrote them.

#### Where should you start?

You do not have to fix every product page at once. Start with your best-selling product, your newest product or one listing that gets views but not sales. Improve the title, update the first paragraph, add missing details, refresh the photos and make the next step easier.

Product pages are part of the whole store experience. If the store structure, navigation, mobile layout and SEO fields are not working together, even strong products can be harder to buy. Marie Glow Studio's [Complete Website and Brand Identity](https://marieglowstudio.com/complete-website-package) covers Shopify setup, a custom homepage, navigation and up to 20 items sorted into products and collections, working from the product images you provide. See [Shopify web design](https://marieglowstudio.com/web-design.html) for the full list.

Clear listing copy works best with strong, consistent imagery. Browse my curated [Visual Branding and Photography Assets](https://benable.com/mariegems/your-curated-visual-branding-photography-assets) for product-photo and website-image resources.

#### Frequently asked questions

**How long should a product description be?**

A product description should be long enough to answer the customer’s real questions. Some simple products may only need a few strong paragraphs and clear details. Custom, handmade, personalized, or higher-consideration products usually need more explanation because customers need to understand options, process, turnaround time, and care instructions.

**What should every Shopify product listing include?**

Every Shopify product listing should include a clear title, helpful photos, customer-focused description, accurate product details, SEO title, meta description, image alt text, price, options, and a clear call to action. If the product is personalized, include instructions for submitting names, photos, logos, or design details.

**How do I make product photos look more trustworthy?**

Use bright natural light or clean artificial lighting, simple backgrounds, clear angles, close-up detail shots, and consistent editing. Show the product in a way that helps customers understand size, color, texture, personalization, and use. Trustworthy product photos do not have to be perfect, but they should be clear and honest.

**Do product listings help with SEO?**

Yes. Product listings can support SEO when the page title, product description, metadata, image alt text, and body content clearly describe what the product is. The goal is to use searchable language naturally so shoppers and search engines can understand the page.

### 10 Signs Your Website Needs a Redesign

URL: https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/10-signs-your-website-needs-a-redesign
Topic: Shopify and Web Design | Published: 2026-06-27

A website can look finished and still be quietly losing you customers. Here's how to tell the difference between 'looks a little dated' and 'is actually costing you sales.' A website needs a redesign when its structure, mobile experience, speed or branding makes it hard for customers to understand the business and take action.

Your website does not have to be perfect to work well. It does need to say clearly who you help, what you offer and what someone should do next. When a site feels confusing, slow, outdated or hard to use, visitors may leave before they understand the value of your business.

#### Why does spotting the signs early matter?

Spotting the signs early lets you fix user experience, outdated design and performance problems before they cost you trust, traffic and conversions. A redesign is not about changing colors or choosing a prettier theme. It improves how your site communicates, guides visitors, supports SEO and helps people take action.

For small business owners, Shopify stores, handmade sellers and service providers, the website is often where trust is built or lost. Social media can introduce people to your brand, but your website is where they decide whether to read more, shop, contact you, join your list or move on.

The goal of a redesign is not to make your site look trendy. The goal is to make it clearer, easier to use and more aligned with your brand, so it is ready to support growth.

#### What are the 10 signs your website needs a redesign?

The ten signs are an outdated or inconsistent design, an unclear offer, a frustrating mobile experience, confusing navigation, slow pages, no leads or sales, missing SEO basics, a site that no longer matches your offers, feeling embarrassed to share it, and pages with no clear next step.

#### 1. Your design looks outdated or no longer matches your brand

One of the clearest signs is that the site no longer matches the quality of your current brand. Maybe your brand colors have changed, your photos are old, your logo looks inconsistent or the branding varies from page to page.

An outdated website can make a strong business look less trustworthy than it is, because visitors often judge the visuals before they read a word. A redesign brings your visuals, messaging and customer experience into line so the site feels like the business you are building now.

#### 2. Visitors cannot quickly tell what you offer

Someone landing on your homepage should understand who you help, what you offer and what step to take next. Vague statements, unclear sections and too many competing offers leave visitors unsure where to go.

This is common in businesses that have grown over time. You add a service, a product, a resource, and eventually the site becomes a collection of pieces instead of a clear path. A redesign reorganizes the content around your current customer journey.

#### 3. Your mobile experience is frustrating

Many visitors see your site from a phone first, especially if they arrive from Pinterest, Instagram, email or Google. Tiny text, buttons that are hard to tap, awkwardly cropped images, confusing menus and pages that need too much pinching or scrolling are all signs of a poor mobile experience.

If your most important content is hard to find on a phone, a redesign may be needed to protect conversions.

#### 4. Your navigation makes people guess

Too many menu options, unclear labels and hidden key pages send visitors away before they explore your offers. On a Shopify store, confusing navigation also hurts product discovery: if shoppers cannot find collections, best sellers, gift ideas or categories, they browse less.

A redesign can simplify the menu, organize your collections or services and create a natural path from the homepage to the next step.

#### 5. Your pages load slowly

Large images, too many apps, heavy video files, outdated code and unnecessary design elements can all slow a page down. You do not have to remove personality to be faster, but the design does need to balance looks with function.

A redesign is a chance to clean up old sections, compress images and remove unused apps.

#### 6. Visitors arrive but do not act

If people visit but do not buy, book or contact you, the problem may be the page experience rather than the traffic. A site that converts usually has clear messaging, strong calls to action, trust signals, easy navigation, helpful details and a simple path forward.

For service providers, that can mean a clear way to book a consultation or explore services. For Shopify stores, it can mean better product pages, collection pages, descriptions, FAQs, reviews and related product suggestions. Start with [how to create product listings that convert](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/how-to-create-product-listings-that-convert.html) if your product pages are the weak spot.

#### 7. Your SEO basics are missing

Missing SEO titles, weak meta descriptions, unclear headings, generic image filenames, duplicate content and poor internal linking make it harder for search engines and visitors to understand your site.

Good SEO does not mean stuffing keywords into every section. It means organized pages with clear titles, useful headings, descriptive copy and logical links between related content. If your site was built quickly or without SEO in mind, a redesign can lay a stronger foundation. The steps in [Shopify SEO for small businesses](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/shopify-seo-for-small-businesses.html) are a good place to begin.

#### 8. Your website no longer matches your offers

Businesses evolve. You may have added a second service, moved from custom products to Shopify design, or shifted from general content to Pinterest marketing. If the site still reflects an older version of your business, visitors may feel confused.

Your website should support what you want to sell now, not only what you used to sell. When your offers change, the homepage, service pages, navigation, calls to action and internal links should change with them.

#### 9. You feel embarrassed to share your website

This sign is easy to overlook, but it matters. If you avoid sharing your website because it does not feel professional, clear or on brand, that hesitation holds back your marketing.

You should feel confident sending people to your site from Pinterest, email, social media, business cards, packaging inserts and everyday conversations.

#### 10. Your pages do not guide visitors to a next step

Every important page needs a purpose. A blog post can lead to a related guide, a service page to a consultation, and a product page to the cart, a related collection or a helpful FAQ.

If pages simply end, visitors may leave even when they liked what they saw. A redesign can add calls to action, internal links, lead magnets, related products and service pathways so the site works harder for you.

#### Should you redesign your website or just refresh it?

If the main problem is cosmetic, start with a refresh. If the main problem is confusion, poor conversions, weak structure or an outdated strategy, a redesign is usually the better choice.

Refresh, redesign or rebuild
| Option | What it changes | Choose it when |
| Refresh | Specific pieces such as images, copy, colors, calls to action or SEO details | The main problem is cosmetic |
| Redesign | Structure, layout, navigation, customer journey and visual system | The main problem is confusion, poor conversions, weak structure or outdated strategy |
| Rebuild | The platform, theme, apps or technical foundation | What you have now no longer supports your goals |

#### What redesign mistakes should you avoid?

These seven redesign mistakes are worth checking for before you start:

- Choosing a theme before clarifying your website goals.
- Redesigning for looks only and ignoring the customer journey.
- Removing important SEO content without a redirect or content plan.
- Hiding key information inside too many dropdowns, sliders or tabs.
- Using vague calls to action like Learn More everywhere.
- Forgetting to test the website on mobile before launch.
- Launching without checking forms, checkout, links and page speed.

#### What should you do before you redesign?

Gather what already works and write down what you want visitors to do, so the redesign protects your existing visibility.

- Review your analytics to find your most visited pages before changing the site structure.
- Write down the top three actions you want visitors to take.
- Audit your navigation and remove pages that no longer support your goals.
- Save your existing SEO titles, meta descriptions, URLs and top-performing content.
- Create a simple launch checklist so forms, links, products, collections and mobile layouts are tested.

If a single page is enough for now, the [Website Starter](https://marieglowstudio.com/website-starter.html) is a mobile-responsive one-page site delivered within 5 business days of a completed intake. It does not include e-commerce, so a store that sells products needs the [Complete Website and Brand Identity](https://marieglowstudio.com/complete-website-package) instead. #### Frequently asked questions

**How often should a small business redesign its website?**

There is no one-size-fits-all timeline. Many businesses review their website every year and consider a larger redesign when their brand, offers, platform, or customer journey has changed significantly.

**Do I need a full website redesign or just a refresh?**

If your site still works well but feels visually outdated, a refresh may be enough. If the structure, navigation, mobile experience, SEO, or conversion path is weak, a full redesign may be more helpful.

**Can a website redesign hurt SEO?**

It can if pages are removed, URLs change without redirects, or important content is deleted. A redesign should include an SEO plan so existing visibility is protected as much as possible.

**What should I fix first if I cannot redesign everything?**

Start with the pages that matter most: your homepage, primary service or product pages, contact page, and highest-traffic blog posts. Improve clarity, calls to action, mobile layout, and internal links first.

### Is Your Website Costing You Customers? Here's How to Find Out in Just 2 Minutes

URL: https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/is-your-website-costing-you-customers
Topic: Shopify and Web Design | Published: 2026-06-27

It looks okay… but why isn't anyone contacting me? Your website may be costing you customers if a first-time visitor cannot quickly understand what you offer, find what they need, trust the business or complete the next step, especially on a phone.

You're not alone. Many small business owners assume that a website that is online is automatically working for them, and that is not always true. Your site should answer questions, build trust, attract visitors through search engines and guide potential customers toward taking action. If it is not doing that, a quick check will show you where to look first.

#### Why does website clarity matter?

Website clarity matters because visitors decide quickly whether they trust your business. If they cannot see what you offer, who it is for or what step to take next, they may leave before ever contacting you, and a confusing site can hurt your conversions, SEO and customer trust.

If your branding also feels inconsistent, start with [Why Cohesive Branding Matters for Small Businesses](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/why-cohesive-branding-matters-for-small-businesses.html).

#### Is your website costing you customers on the homepage?

It may be, if a first-time visitor cannot understand your business within a few seconds. Ask yourself:

- Can someone tell what I offer right away?
- Is my main call to action easy to find?
- Does my homepage reflect my current brand?

If the homepage feels outdated, cluttered or unclear, review the layout and the messaging. The homepage has a direct effect on your website conversion rate, because people decide fast whether an offer feels clear and relevant.

#### Does your navigation feel effortless?

It should. Visitors should not have to hunt for information. Your menu needs to make it easy to find your products, services, blog, contact page and important business information.

Confusing navigation makes simple actions harder to find, while simple navigation helps visitors feel confident and helps search engines understand your website.

#### Does your website build trust?

People buy from businesses they trust, and trust builders include testimonials, clear contact information, consistent branding, professional visuals and helpful website copy. These details also make your business feel reliable and easy to come back to.

If your visuals, colors, messaging or customer experience feel disconnected, read [Branding Mistakes Small Businesses Should Avoid](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/branding-mistakes-small-businesses-should-avoid.html).

#### Does every product or service page have a purpose?

Each page should answer four questions:

- What is this?
- Who is it for?
- Why does it matter?
- What should the visitor do next?

If your pages only list features without explaining benefits, visitors may leave without buying or booking. Benefit-first copy can reduce usability problems and make the next step obvious. For product pages, see [how to create product listings that convert](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/how-to-create-product-listings-that-convert.html). If you are earlier in your journey, [How to Start a Product-Based Business From Home](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/how-to-start-a-product-based-business-from-home.html) is a helpful next read.

#### Is your website costing you customers on mobile?

Many people will visit from a phone, so check whether your text is easy to read, buttons are easy to tap, images load properly and the layout looks clean.

If the mobile version feels cramped or hard to tap, your conversion rate may suffer even when the desktop version looks polished. A mobile-friendly website creates a better experience and can help more visitors take action.

#### Are your SEO basics in place?

Your website needs basic SEO so people can find you online. The basics are:

- Unique page titles
- Helpful meta descriptions
- Image alt text
- Blog content that answers customer questions

Even small updates to titles, descriptions and alt text help search engines understand what your site offers. For the full set of steps, read [Shopify SEO for small businesses](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/shopify-seo-for-small-businesses.html), or see how search works beyond Google in [Pinterest SEO for beginners](https://marieglowstudio.com/blog/pinterest-seo-beginners-guide.html).

#### How do you run a two-minute website check?

Open your site on your phone and pretend you are a new visitor. See whether you can explain the business and find the main product or service within a few seconds. Then work through six areas:

- Homepage
- Navigation
- Mobile experience
- SEO basics
- Product and service pages
- Trust builders

As you go, look for the places where visitors may hesitate, back up or leave. Small changes to copy, layout and navigation add up over time, so choose one page to improve first and keep the next step manageable.

Look for unclear messaging, hard-to-find navigation, slow loading, mobile problems, missing trust information, and a checkout or contact process that feels confusing.
